# Projects and the public site

A project is one product with its own public site. The code calls a project a "client". All the data of a project stays in that project: posts, contacts, boards, stages, tags, release notes, testimonials, settings and API tokens.

## Create a project

The setup page and `php artisan fp:install` create the first project of the owner. A new user on an open instance creates a project during onboarding.

To create a project, give:

- a name,
- a subdomain. The subdomain uses lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, for example `acme`. It must be unique on the instance.

These subdomains are reserved: `admin`, `api`, `app`, `assets`, `blog`, `cdn`, `dashboard`, `dev`, `docs`, `help`, `mail`, `mcp`, `smtp`, `staging`, `static`, `status`, `support` and `www`.

When the app creates a project, it also creates:

- a publishable key and an identity secret for the widget,
- six default stages (read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md)),
- one public board with the name `Feature Requests`,
- the testimonial settings: rating off, automation off, and a default email text,
- an admin contact for the user.

To create one more project, open the project selector at the top of the sidebar and select **New project**. The form at `/onboarding/project` opens. To go back without a new project, click **Cancel**.

## Switch projects

A user can belong to more than one project. The project selector at the top of the sidebar changes the active project. The dashboard keeps the active project in the session. If the session has no project, the dashboard opens the first project of the user.

Only the code that creates a project adds a user to it. No screen adds a second user to a project. Team members (invitations and roles) are a later feature.

## Rename a project

1. In the dashboard, open **Settings > Project**.
2. Change the fields.
3. Click **Save project**.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| Name | Required. 255 characters or fewer. |
| Website | Optional. 255 characters or fewer, for example `example.com`. The public site shows a "Back to" link to this address. Leave it empty to remove the link. |
| Logo | Optional. JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP, 1 MB or less. SVG is not accepted. |

The subdomain of a project cannot change after creation. No form or route changes it.

## The public site

The public site of a project is at `https://<subdomain>.<APP_DOMAIN>`, for example `https://acme.feedback.example.com`. The app finds the project from the host name.

| Path | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `/` | The four newest release notes and the five newest published posts. |
| `/posts` | The published posts. A contact can filter by a public board and sort by date or by votes (`sort_by` is `created_at__DESC`, `created_at__ASC`, `votes_count__DESC` or `votes_count__ASC`). Another `sort_by` value shows the newest posts first. Completed posts are hidden unless the visitor asks for them. |
| `/posts/{id}` | One published post with its comments and votes. |
| `/roadmap` | The roadmap. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md#the-public-roadmap). |
| `/release-notes` | The release notes that have a publication date. |
| `/release-notes/{slug}` | One release note. |
| `/testimonials` | The approved testimonials, and the testimonials of the signed-in contact. |

Anyone can read these pages. To post, vote, comment or write a testimonial, a contact must be signed in.

The public site shows only the posts of public boards. The board filter lists only public boards. A post of a private board does not show on `/`, `/posts`, `/roadmap` or the roadmap iframe. Its page returns 404, and a contact cannot vote or comment on it.

If the project has a website in **Settings > Project**, the public site shows a link back to that website.

## How a contact signs in

A contact has no password. A contact signs in with a signed link to `/authenticate/{uuid}`. The link holds an expiry and a signature.

| Link source | Lifetime |
|---|---|
| The widget, the **Public Site** link and **View site as contact** in the dashboard | 24 hours |
| An email to the contact | 7 days |

The app refuses a link with no expiry, a bad signature, or a contact of another project. After the sign-in, the app goes only to a path on the same host. The sign-in link of the admin contact of a deactivated user returns 404.

The public site has no sign-up form for contacts. Contacts come from the widget, the REST API and the MCP server. Read [The embeddable widget](widget.md) and [Contacts and revenue](contacts.md).

## Preview the public site

The **Public Site** link in the sidebar of the dashboard opens the public site of the active project. It signs you in as your admin contact. When you post or comment on the public site, you act as this admin contact.

## Custom domains

Custom domains are not supported. The public site of a project is only on its subdomain. A host outside `APP_DOMAIN` gets 404.

## Deactivated users

If every user of a project is deactivated, the public site, the iframes and the widget of the project stop. The public site returns 404 and the widget gets 401. A project with one active user, or with no user, keeps them. Read [The admin area](admin-area.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/boards.md

# Boards

A board is a group of posts in a project, for example `Feature Requests` or `Bugs`. Each post belongs to one board. Each project starts with one public board with the name `Feature Requests`.

All the boards of a project share the stages. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md).

## Manage boards

Open **Boards** in the sidebar. The page lists the boards in order, with the number of posts on each board.

| Field | Rules | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Required, 255 characters or fewer | The name of the board. The app makes the slug from the name. |
| Public | On or off | A public board shows in the board filter of the public site and of the roadmap. |

A new board goes to the end of the list.

### Delete a board

When you delete a board, the app moves its posts to the first other board of the project. A project must keep at least one board. If you try to delete the last board, the app shows the error `You must keep at least one board.`

## Where a new post goes

- A post from the dashboard, the REST API or the MCP server can name a board with `board_id`.
- If a post names no board, the app puts it on the first board of the project.
- A post from the public site goes to the first board of the project.

## The kanban board of a board

Each row of the **Boards** page links to the kanban board of that board, at `/board?board=<id>`. The kanban board shows one board at a time, with a board switcher. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md#the-kanban-board).

## Filter the posts by board

The **Posts** page of the dashboard has a tab for each board, and a **Manage boards** link.

The public site and the roadmap have a filter with the public boards only. Read the warning in [Projects and the public site](projects-and-public-site.md#the-public-site).

## Embed the roadmap

The **Boards** page shows an iframe snippet for the roadmap of the project. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md#embed-the-roadmap).

## Boards in the API and the MCP server

The REST API and the MCP server use the field `board_id` to write a post to a board. The REST API list of posts can filter by `board_id`. The board must belong to the project of the token.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/posts-votes-and-comments.md

# Posts, votes and comments

A post is one piece of feedback, for example a feature request or a bug.

## Where posts come from

| Source | Author | Published | Other effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| The public site | The signed-in contact | Yes, at once | The author votes for the post. The first user of the project gets an email. |
| The dashboard (**Posts > New**) | The contact that you choose, or your admin contact | No | None |
| The REST API or the MCP server | No contact | No | None |

Each new post starts in the first `open` stage of the project, with the status `pending`. The REST API and the MCP server can give another status.

For each new post, the app also sends the `post.created` webhook event and a Slack message, if they are set. Read [Webhooks and Slack](webhooks-and-slack.md).

### A post from the public site

A signed-in contact fills in:

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| Title | Required |
| Content | Required |
| Tags | Optional. Tags of the project. |
| Attachments | Optional. Up to 10 files, 10 MB each. Types: `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `gif`, `webp`, `pdf`, `doc`, `docx` and `txt`. |

The dashboard and the public site show the attachments of a post.

## Publish and archive

- **Publish** sets the publication date of a post. Only a published post shows on the public site.
- **Unpublish** removes the publication date.
- **Archive** hides the post from the post list of the dashboard and from the roadmap.
- **Unarchive** shows the post again.

The post list of the public site does not filter archived posts. A published post that is archived still shows on `/posts`.

A post from the dashboard, the REST API or the MCP server is not published. Publish it in the dashboard before customers can see it.

## The post list of the dashboard

Open **Posts** in the sidebar. The list shows 12 posts on each page.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Search | Finds the text in the title or the content. |
| Board tabs | Show the posts of one board. |
| Tags | Show the posts with the tags that you choose. |
| Show Completed | Also shows the posts with the status `completed`. |
| Show archived | Also shows the archived posts. |
| Sort | Sorts by date, or by priority (**Highest Priority**, **Lowest Priority**). |

### The priority score

The priority score of a post is the number of votes plus the sum of the MRR of the voters:

```text
score = number of votes + sum of the MRR of each voter
```

A vote from a contact with a high MRR raises the score more. Read [Contacts and revenue](contacts.md) to send the MRR of your customers.

## Votes

A signed-in contact can vote for a post on the public site, and remove the vote. Contacts can also vote for release notes and testimonials.

### Vote for a contact

If a customer asks for a feature by email or in a call, add the vote for the customer:

1. Open the post in the dashboard.
2. Open **Votes**.
3. Choose the contact.
4. Add the vote.

If the contact has a vote on the post already, the app shows the error `That contact has already voted on this post.`

## Comments

Contacts can comment on posts, release notes and testimonials on the public site. A comment can have up to 5 photos, 5 MB each, of the types `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `gif` and `webp`.

A user can reply to a post in the dashboard. The reply comes from the admin contact of the user.

When someone comments on a post, the author of the post gets an email. The author gets no email for a comment of their own. Read [Notifications and weekly reports](notifications-and-weekly-reports.md).

## Notes

Each post has private notes for the team. The notes do not show on the public site. The REST API returns the notes in the `notes` field.

## Merge duplicate posts

If two posts ask for the same thing, merge the duplicate into the main post:

1. Open the duplicate post.
2. In the merge panel, choose the main post.
3. Confirm the merge.

The merge does these steps in one database transaction:

1. It removes the votes of the duplicate from contacts that voted for the main post already.
2. It moves the other votes to the main post.
3. It moves the comments to the main post.
4. It moves the attachments to the main post.
5. It deletes the duplicate.

CAUTION: Make sure that you choose the correct main post. You cannot undo a merge.

## Change the stage

Move a post to another stage on the kanban board, or choose a stage on the page of the post. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/stages-and-roadmap.md

# Stages and the roadmap

A stage is one step of the status pipeline of a post, for example `Planned` or `In Progress`. The dashboard calls a stage a "status". All the boards of a project share the stages.

## The default stages

Each new project gets these six stages:

| Stage | Type | On the roadmap | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open | `open` | No | `#94a3b8` |
| Under Review | `open` | No | `#eab308` |
| Planned | `planned` | Yes | `#6366f1` |
| In Progress | `active` | Yes | `#3b82f6` |
| Complete | `complete` | Yes | `#22c55e` |
| Closed | `closed` | No | `#6b7280` |

## Stage types and the status of a post

The stage is the source of truth for the progress of a post. Each post also has a `status` field for the REST API, the MCP server and the metrics. The app keeps the two fields in step.

| Stage type | Status of the post |
|---|---|
| `open` | `pending` |
| `planned` | `in_progress` |
| `active` | `in_progress` |
| `complete` | `completed` |
| `closed` | `pending` |

When the REST API or the MCP server sets a status, the app moves the post to the first stage of the matching type:

| Status | Stage type |
|---|---|
| `pending` | `open` |
| `in_progress` | `active` |
| `completed` | `complete` |

## The kanban board

The kanban board shows the stages as columns. It shows the posts of one board at a time. Open it from the **Boards** page.

Drag a post to another column to change its stage. The change saves at once.

## Manage the stages

On the kanban board, open **Manage statuses**.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| Name | Required, 255 characters or fewer |
| Color | Required, a hex color with six digits, for example `#22c55e` |
| Type | Required. One of `open`, `planned`, `active`, `complete` or `closed`. |
| On the roadmap | On or off |

You can also change the order of the stages.

When you delete a stage, the app moves its posts to the first `open` stage of the project. You cannot delete the only `complete` stage. The app shows the error `You cannot delete the only "complete" status.`

## What happens when a post changes stage

These effects occur only when a user changes the stage in the dashboard, and only if the stage is different:

1. The app sends the `post.status_changed` webhook event.
2. The app posts a Slack message, if Slack is set.
3. If the new stage has the type `complete`, and the post was not complete before:
   - the author and each voter get the email "has been completed",
   - the app sends the `post.completed` webhook event,
   - the app can ask the author for a testimonial. Read [Testimonials](testimonials.md#ask-for-a-testimonial-automatically).
4. For any other stage, the author and each voter get an email with the new stage.

A status change from the REST API or the MCP server moves the post to the first stage of the matching type. Then the app does the same steps as for a stage change in the dashboard. If the status does not change, the app does nothing.

## The public roadmap

The roadmap is at `/roadmap` on the public site of the project. It shows:

- the stages that are on the roadmap, in their order,
- in each stage, the published posts that are not archived, with the most votes first.

The visitor can filter the roadmap by a public board.

### Embed the roadmap

The roadmap also has an iframe version at `/iframe/roadmap`. The **Boards** page of the dashboard shows the snippet:

```html
<iframe src="https://acme.feedback.example.com/iframe/roadmap" width="100%" height="600" style="border:0" title="Roadmap"></iframe>
```

The iframe routes allow framing on any site. They send the header `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/tags.md

# Tags

A tag is a label in a project. You can put tags on posts, contacts and release notes. The title of a tag is unique in a project.

## Manage tags in the dashboard

Open **Tags** in the sidebar. The list shows the number of posts and contacts of each tag. You can create a tag, and open a tag to see its posts and contacts.

Use tags to filter:

- the **Posts** list,
- the **Contacts** list.

A contact can choose tags of the project when they write a post on the public site.

## Tags in the REST API and the MCP server

The REST API and the MCP server can list, create, rename and delete tags. Read [Tags](../api/tags.md) in the API section.

- To set the tags of a record, send `tags` with a list of tag IDs. The list replaces all the tags of the record.
- To filter a list of posts, contacts or release notes, send `tag` with the title of a tag.

The REST API and the MCP server can delete a tag. The app first removes the tag from its posts, contacts and release notes. Then it deletes the tag.

## Rename or delete a tag in the dashboard

Open **Tags**, then open a tag.

- To rename the tag, change the title in the **Rename** field and click **Save**. Two tags of a project cannot have the same title.
- To delete the tag, click **Delete tag** and confirm. The app removes the tag from its posts, contacts and release notes, then deletes it.

The dashboard uses the same rules as the REST API and the MCP server.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/contacts.md

# Contacts and revenue

A contact is a customer of one project. Contacts post, vote, comment and write testimonials on the public site. Each contact has a name, an email, an avatar, an MRR, an LTV, tags, notes and custom attributes.

## Where contacts come from

The dashboard has no form to create a contact. Contacts come from:

| Source | Match | Read more |
|---|---|---|
| The widget (`pilgrim.js`) | The email, in the project | [The embeddable widget](widget.md) |
| `POST /api/public/v1/contacts` | The email, in the project | [Contacts](../api/contacts.md) |
| `POST /api/public/v1/init` | The email, in the project | [Init](../api/init.md) |
| The MCP tool `create_contact` | The email, in the project | [MCP tools reference](../mcp/tools-reference.md#create_contact) |

Each source creates the contact if the email is new in the project. If the email exists, the source updates the contact. The widget updates an existing contact only with a valid identity hash. Read [The embeddable widget](widget.md#identity-verification).

If a contact has no avatar, the app makes an image with the initials of the contact.

## Revenue weighting

Each contact has two revenue fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mrr` | The monthly recurring revenue of the customer. |
| `ltv` | The lifetime value of the customer. |

Send the values from your app through the widget, the REST API or the MCP server. A user can also change them on the edit page of a contact.

The values change these parts of the dashboard:

- The priority score of a post is the number of votes plus the sum of the MRR of the voters. Sort the **Posts** list by **Highest Priority** to see the posts with the most revenue first.
- The **Contacts** list and the page of a contact mark the top 10 contacts by MRR. They also mark the top 10 contacts by LTV.
- The REST API and the MCP server can sort the contacts by `mrr` or `ltv`.

## Custom attributes

A contact can have custom attributes, for example a plan name or a company size. The app stores them in the `metadata` field of the contact.

- The widget stores each key of the contact object that is not `name`, `email`, `mrr`, `ltv` or `top_customer`.
- The REST API and the MCP server store each unknown field, and the keys of a `metadata` object.

When the metadata of a contact changes, a queued job adds each new key to the list of attributes of the project. The **Contacts** list uses this list to filter the contacts by an attribute value.

To make the list again from all the contacts, run:

```bash
php artisan fp:sync-contact-attributes
```

The REST API and the MCP server apply these limits to the metadata:

- A key cannot start with `pilgrim_`. The app keeps these keys for itself.
- 50 keys or fewer, nested keys included.
- 3 levels of nesting or fewer.
- 16 KB or less as JSON.

The app stores two keys of its own: `pilgrim_last_login` (the last widget login) and `pilgrim_last_release_note` (the last release note that the widget opened for the contact). The API responses do not show these keys.

## The contacts list

Open **Contacts** in the sidebar. The list does not show the admin contacts of the users. You can:

- filter by tags,
- filter by the value of a custom attribute,
- sort the list.

Each row shows the number of posts, comments and votes of the contact.

## The page of a contact

The page of a contact shows:

- the number of sessions. The app counts one session a day at most, for each sign-in through the widget or the `init` API endpoint,
- the five newest posts, comments and votes,
- the tags,
- the top MRR and top LTV marks.

On the edit page, a user can change the name, the email, the notes, the MRR, the LTV, the tags and the custom attributes.

### View the site as a contact

**View site as contact** opens the public site and signs you in as this contact. Use it to see what the contact sees. While you are signed in as the contact, your posts, votes and comments come from the contact.

## Contacts in the API

The REST API and the MCP server can list, get, create and update contacts. They cannot delete a contact. Read [Contacts](../api/contacts.md) in the API section.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/release-notes.md

# Release notes

A release note is a changelog entry of a project. Contacts can read, vote and comment on release notes on the public site.

## Create a release note in the dashboard

Open **Release Notes** in the sidebar, then create a note.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| Title | Required |
| Content | Required |
| Publication date | Optional (`published_at`). Leave it empty to save a draft. |

The app makes the slug from the title and the date of creation, for example `new-dashboard-20261117` for the title "New dashboard". The public URL of the note is `/release-notes/<slug>` on the public site.

## Publish and unpublish

The publication date (`published_at`) is the only switch. A note with a publication date is published. A note without one is a draft.

The page of a note has one of these buttons:

- **Publish** (for a draft): sets the publication date to the current time. If the note already has a date, the note keeps it.
- **Unpublish** (for a published note): clears the publication date. The note becomes a draft.

## What the public site shows

The public site, the widget and the iframe show only the published notes. A draft gets 404 on the public site.

## Release notes from the REST API or the MCP server

The REST API and the MCP server create a draft by default. They can change the title, the content and the tags.

To publish or unpublish a note, send `published`:

| Value | Result |
|---|---|
| `true` | The note is published. If the note has no publication date, it gets the current time. |
| `false` | The publication date is cleared. The note becomes a draft. |

Read [Release notes in the API](../api/release-notes.md) and the [MCP tools reference](../mcp/tools-reference.md).

## The release notes in your app

The widget can show the release notes of the project in an iframe in your app. It can also open the newest note one time for each contact. Read [The embeddable widget](widget.md#release-notes).

The iframe is at `/iframe/release-notes` on the public site.

## Comments on release notes

When a contact comments on a release note, the user who wrote the note gets an email. Read [Notifications and weekly reports](notifications-and-weekly-reports.md).

## Edit a release note

The **Edit** link on the page of a note opens a form for the title and the content. The dashboard has no delete for a release note.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/testimonials.md

# Testimonials

A testimonial is a text from a customer, with an optional star rating from 1 to 5. A testimonial shows on the public site after a user approves it.

## Where testimonials come from

| Source | Fields | Approved at creation | Author |
|---|---|---|---|
| The public site (`/testimonials/create`) | Title, description, rating | No | The signed-in contact |
| The widget | Description, rating | No | The contact of the widget, or `Anonymous User` |
| The dashboard (**Testimonials > New**) | Title, description, user name, subtitle, contact, rating | Yes | The contact that you choose, or none |
| The REST API or the MCP server | Description, user name, rating, contact | No | The contact that you give, or none |
| A Senja CSV file (**Testimonials > Import**) | Title, description, user name, subtitle, avatar, rating, date | Yes | None |

On the public site, a contact can edit their own testimonials. A contact sees their own testimonials before approval.

The widget endpoint accepts 5 testimonials a minute from each IP address.

## Import testimonials from Senja

You can import a CSV export from [Senja](https://senja.io). Each row with text becomes an approved testimonial.

1. In Senja, export your testimonials as a CSV file.
2. In the dashboard, open **Testimonials**.
3. Click **Import**.
4. In **CSV file**, select the file.
5. Click **Import**.

The page then shows "Imported N testimonials (D already imported, M skipped)."

### The columns

| Senja column | Testimonial field |
|---|---|
| `text` | The description. A row without text is skipped. |
| `customer_name` | The user name. If it is empty, the user name is `Anonymous`. |
| `customer_tagline` | The subtitle |
| `customer_company` | The subtitle, if `customer_tagline` is empty |
| `customer_avatar` | The avatar. The app copies the image of an `https` URL of 255 characters or fewer. Read [Avatars of imported testimonials](#avatars-of-imported-testimonials). |
| `rating` | The rating, from 1 to 5. Another value, for example `0`, gives no rating. |
| `title` | The title |
| `date` | The creation date and the approval date. If the date is empty or not valid, the app uses the time of the import. |

The file must have the columns `text` and `customer_name`. If one is missing, the app refuses the file with "This doesn't look like a Senja CSV export — the expected columns are missing."

### Limits of the import

- The file is a CSV file of 2 MB or less.
- The file has 5000 rows or fewer. If the file has more rows, the app imports no row. Split the file and import each part.
- The app skips a row with text of more than 5000 characters. It also skips a row with a title, a user name or a subtitle of more than 255 characters.
- The app keeps the rating of a row also when the **Rating** setting is off.
- The imported testimonials have no contact.
- The app skips a row that is already in the project. Read [Import the same file again](#import-the-same-file-again).
- A project can run one import at a time. If an import of the project runs, the app refuses a second import with "Another import of testimonials is running. Try again in a minute."
- A user can start 10 imports each minute.

### Import the same file again

You can import a new Senja export that has the rows of an earlier export. The app skips each row that is already in the project. The result shows the count of these rows as "already imported".

A row is already in the project when a testimonial of the project has the same user name and the same description. The Senja export has no ID for each row, so the app compares these two values.

- If you edit the description of an imported testimonial, the next import adds the row from Senja again.
- If two people wrote the same text, and they have the same name, the app imports only the first row.
- The app also finds the testimonials that an import made before this change.

### Avatars of imported testimonials

The app copies each avatar to its own storage. The public site does not load images from Senja.

The copy runs on the queue after the import. Until the copy is done, the testimonial shows an avatar with the initials of the user name. If no queue worker runs, the copy does not occur. Read [Queues and the scheduler](../self-hosting/queues-and-scheduler.md).

The app does not copy an avatar in these cases. The testimonial then keeps the initials avatar.

- The URL is not `https`, or it has more than 255 characters.
- The host of the URL has a private or local address.
- The server answers with a redirect or an error, or it does not answer in 10 seconds.
- The image is larger than 1 MB.
- The file is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image. The app reads the type from the file content.

When a copy fails, the app writes "Could not copy the avatar of an imported testimonial." to the log, with the testimonial ID and the reason.

The testimonials of imports that ran before this change keep the URL of the Senja image.

## Approve a testimonial

Open the testimonial in the dashboard. Then:

- **Approve** sets the approval date. The public site shows the testimonial.
- The second button removes the approval date. The public site hides the testimonial again.

The REST API and the MCP server approve a testimonial when you set `approved_at`.

The **Testimonials** list can show all, the approved or the pending testimonials.

## Testimonial settings

Open **Settings > Testimonials**.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Rating | Off | If on, the forms of the public site, the widget and the dashboard require a rating from 1 to 5. If off, these forms store no rating. |
| Automation | Off | If on, the app can ask for a testimonial by email when a post is complete. |
| Email text | A default text | The text of the request email. 5000 characters or fewer. |

## Ask for a testimonial automatically

If **Automation** is on, the app can send the email "Share your experience with us!". It does this when a user moves a post to a stage of the type `complete`. The app sends the email to the author of the post only if all these conditions are true:

1. The post has an author.
2. The author has no testimonial in the project yet.
3. No other post of the author became complete in the last month.

The button in the email opens `/testimonials/create` on the public site and signs in the contact. The link stays valid for 7 days.

### The email text

Put the token `{testimonialButton}` in the email text. The app puts the **Leave a Testimonial** button in that place. The text before the token goes above the button, and the text after the token goes below it. If the text has no token, the app puts the button at the end.

The app prints the email text as plain text. It does not fill in variables. The default text starts with `Hi {{ $contact->name ?? $contact->email }},`, and the email shows this expression as it is. To greet the customer correctly, replace the expression with your own greeting.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/notifications-and-weekly-reports.md

# Notifications and weekly reports

Feedback Pilgrim sends all its notifications by email. The notifications go through the queue, so a queue worker must run. Read [Queues and the scheduler](../self-hosting/queues-and-scheduler.md) and [Mail](../self-hosting/mail.md).

## Emails to contacts

| Email | When | Recipients |
|---|---|---|
| Post completed | A user moves a post to a `complete` stage, and the post was not complete before. | The author of the post and each voter |
| Post status changed (subject `Update on "<title>"`) | A user moves a post to another stage that is not `complete`. | The author of the post and each voter |
| Post commented | Someone comments on a post. | The author of the post, if the comment is not from the author |
| Testimonial request (subject `Share your experience with us!`) | A post becomes complete and the automation is on. | The author of the post. Read [Testimonials](testimonials.md#ask-for-a-testimonial-automatically). |

The emails to contacts come from the sender address of the instance, with the name of the project. If the project has a verified sending domain, they come from that domain. Read [Send email from your domain](sending-domain.md).

The app sends one email to each voter, also if the contact voted more than one time. The author of the post does not get the voter email in addition.

The button in an email to a contact opens the public site and signs in the contact. The link stays valid for 7 days.

A status change from the REST API or the MCP server sends the same emails. Read [Stages and the roadmap](stages-and-roadmap.md#what-happens-when-a-post-changes-stage).

## Emails to users

| Email | When | Recipients |
|---|---|---|
| New post | A contact writes a post on the public site. | The first user of the project, unless the post is from the admin contact of that user |
| Release note commented | A contact comments on a release note. | The user who wrote the release note |
| Weekly report (subject `Weekly Report for <project>`) | Every Monday at 09:00 | Each user of each project |

## The weekly report

The scheduler runs `php artisan fp:weekly` every Monday at 09:00. The app uses the time zone `UTC`.

The command does two steps:

1. It computes the report of the previous week, from Monday to Sunday, for each project, and stores it.
2. It sends the report by email to each user of each project.

The report has these values:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Posts Created | The new posts of the project in the week, from all sources. |
| Posts Completed | The posts with the status `completed` that changed in the week. |
| Active Contacts | The contacts with a post, a comment or a vote in the week. |
| Total Engagement Events | The number of contact logins in the week. |
| Top Post Creators | The contacts with the most posts. |
| Most Active Commenters | The contacts with the most comments. |

The week starts on Monday. The scheduled run on Monday at 09:00 reports the full week that ended on Sunday. A run by hand also reports the previous week.

To make and send the report by hand, run:

```bash
php artisan fp:weekly
```

The dashboard also shows the activity of the last 7 days: the contact logins by day, the top contacts and a summary.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/sending-domain.md

# Send email from your domain

By default, the emails to your contacts come from the sender address of the instance, with the name of your project. With a sending domain, these emails come from an address on your own domain, for example `feedback@example.com`.

The emails go through Amazon SES. SES signs each email with DKIM for your domain, so the emails pass DMARC for your domain.

## Which emails use the sending domain

The sending domain applies to the emails to contacts:

- Post completed
- Post status changed
- Post commented
- Testimonial request

The emails to users do not change. For example, the new post email, the weekly report and the password reset still come from the sender address of the instance. Read [Notifications and weekly reports](notifications-and-weekly-reports.md) for the list of emails.

## Before you start

- The operator of the instance must set the SES keys. If the keys are not set, the connection of a domain fails. Read [Mail](../self-hosting/mail.md#sending-domains-for-projects).
- You need access to the DNS records of your domain.

## Connect a domain

1. In the dashboard, open **Settings > Email**.
2. In **Domain**, enter your domain, for example `example.com`.
3. In **Sender address**, enter the part before the `@`. The default is `feedback`.
4. Look at the **From** line below the fields. It shows the sender of the emails.
5. Click **Connect domain**. The page shows the DNS records.
6. Add each DNS record at your DNS provider.
7. Wait for SES to find the records. To check the domain at once, click **Check now**.

The replies of your contacts go to the sender address. Use an address that someone reads.

### The domain

- The app removes `https://`, `www.`, a path and a final dot. For example, `https://www.Example.com/path` becomes `example.com`.
- You can use a subdomain, for example `mail.example.com`.
- Free email domains do not work: `gmail.com`, `outlook.com`, `hotmail.com`, `yahoo.com`, `icloud.com`, `proton.me` and `aol.com`.
- The domain of the instance and the domain of its sender address do not work. Their subdomains also do not work.
- A domain can belong to one project only, in the whole instance.

### The sender address

The sender address is 64 characters or fewer. It can have lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes, plus signs and underscores. The app changes uppercase letters to lowercase.

## The DNS records

The page shows six records. In the table, `example.com` is your domain and `<region>` is the SES region of the instance.

| Purpose | Type | Name | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| DKIM (three records) | CNAME | `<token>._domainkey.example.com` | `<token>.dkim.amazonses.com` |
| MAIL FROM | MX | `bounce.example.com` | `10 feedback-smtp.<region>.amazonses.com` |
| MAIL FROM | TXT | `bounce.example.com` | `v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all` |
| DMARC | TXT | `_dmarc.example.com` | `v=DMARC1; p=none;` |

Each record has a copy button. Copy the exact names and values from the page, because each domain gets its own DKIM tokens.

- SES verifies the domain with the three DKIM records.
- The MAIL FROM records set `bounce.example.com` as the bounce address. If these records are missing, SES uses its own bounce address.
- The DMARC record is a suggestion. If your domain already has a DMARC record, keep your record. A domain must have only one DMARC record.

## The states of a domain

| State | What it means | The emails come from |
|---|---|---|
| Pending | SES did not find the DKIM records yet. | The sender address of the instance |
| Verified | SES verified the domain. | The sender address on your domain |
| Verification lost | SES verified the domain before, but it does not verify the domain now. | The sender address of the instance |
| Failed | SES looked for the DKIM records for 72 hours and did not find them. | The sender address of the instance |

The app checks a pending domain every 10 minutes. It checks a verified domain again one time each day. It does not check a failed domain.

## If the domain failed

1. Click **Try again**. The app makes new DKIM records.
2. At your DNS provider, replace the old DKIM CNAME records with the new records.
3. Wait for SES to find the new records, or click **Check now**.

## Remove a domain

1. Click **Remove domain**.
2. Confirm the dialog.

The app removes the domain from the project and from SES. The emails come from the sender address of the instance again. The app does not change your DNS records. If you do not use the records again, remove them at your DNS provider.

## Limits

- A project has one sending domain. To use another domain, remove the domain first. Then connect the new domain.
- The From name is the name of the project. To change it, open **Settings > Project**.
- **Connect domain**, **Check now**, **Try again** and **Remove domain** accept 5 requests each minute for each user.
- If the SES account of the instance is in the SES sandbox, SES sends only to verified addresses. The operator must request production access from AWS.
- The app does not change DNS records. You add and remove the records yourself.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/widget.md

# The embeddable widget

The widget is the script `pilgrim.js`. Add it to your own app. The widget can:

- sign in the users of your app on the public site of your project, without a second login,
- create or update the contact of each user, with the MRR, the LTV and custom attributes,
- show the release notes in an iframe, and open the newest note one time for each contact,
- show the testimonial form in an iframe.

The widget is not the REST API. It uses the publishable key of the project, not an API token.

## Keys

Open **Settings > Embed Widget** in the dashboard.

| Key | Format | Public | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publishable key | `pk_` and 32 letters and digits | Yes | Identifies the project. It gives no API access. You can put it in HTML. |
| Identity secret | 64 hexadecimal characters | No | Your server uses it to sign the email of the signed-in user. |

WARNING: Keep the identity secret on your server. Never put it in HTML or JavaScript. With the secret, anyone can sign in as any contact of your project.

The app stores the identity secret encrypted with `APP_KEY`. To make a new secret, click **Regenerate secret**. After that, a user fails the verification until your app uses the new secret.

## Add the widget

1. Add the script to the pages of your app. Use the `pilgrim.js` of your instance:

   ```html
   <script src="https://feedback.example.com/pilgrim.js" data-client="pk_your_publishable_key"></script>
   ```

2. On your server, make the identity hash of the email of the signed-in user:

   ```php
   $userHash = hash_hmac('sha256', strtolower(trim($user->email)), $identitySecret);
   ```

   In Node.js:

   ```js
   import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'

   // The same rule as PHP strtolower(trim($email)).
   const normalizedEmail = email
     .replace(/^[ \t\n\r\0\x0B]+|[ \t\n\r\0\x0B]+$/g, '')
     .replace(/[A-Z]/g, (letter) => letter.toLowerCase())

   const userHash = createHmac('sha256', identitySecret).update(normalizedEmail).digest('hex')
   ```

   The app removes only the spaces, tabs, line breaks, NUL and vertical tabs at the start and at the end of the email. It changes only the letters `A` to `Z` to lowercase. Do not use `trim()` and `toLowerCase()` of JavaScript. They also change other whitespace and the Unicode letters, and then the hash does not match.

3. Call `pilgrim()` at the end of the `<body>`:

   ```html
   <script>
     pilgrim({
       contact: {
         email: "jane@example.com", // required
         name: "Jane Doe",          // optional
         mrr: 49,                   // optional
         ltv: 1200,                 // optional
         plan: "pro",               // optional, a custom attribute
       },
       userHash: "<hash-from-your-server>",
       releaseNotes: { show: true, open: true }, // optional
       testimonials: true,                       // optional
     })
   </script>
   ```

4. Add these attributes to links or buttons in your app:

   | Attribute | What a click does |
   |---|---|
   | `data-pilgrim-link` | Opens the public site. With a valid `userHash`, it signs in the user. |
   | `data-pilgrim-release-notes` | Opens the release notes iframe. |
   | `data-pilgrim-testimonials` | Opens the testimonial form iframe. |

The widget reads the URL of your instance from the `src` of its own script tag. One build of `pilgrim.js` works on every host.

## What the widget sends

`pilgrim()` sends a `POST` request to `/api/v1/init` on your instance, with the header `Authorization: Bearer <publishable key>`. The body has `contact`, `releaseNotes`, `testimonials` and `user_hash`.

| Field of the contact | What the app does with it |
|---|---|
| `email` | Required. The app finds the contact by email in the project. |
| `name` | The name of the contact. |
| `mrr`, `ltv` | The revenue of the customer. Read [Contacts and revenue](contacts.md#revenue-weighting). |
| `avatar` | The URL of an avatar image. |
| Other keys | Custom attributes. The app ignores `top_customer`. |

The keys `show` and `open` of `releaseNotes` are both optional.

## Identity verification

The publishable key is public. Thus, the key alone does not prove who the user is. The identity hash (`userHash`) proves the email of the user.

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| A correct `userHash` | The app creates or updates the contact and signs it in. |
| A wrong `userHash` | `403` with `{"error": "Identity verification failed"}`. |
| No `userHash`, and verification is required | `403` with `{"error": "Identity verification failed"}`. |
| No `userHash`, verification not required, new email | The app creates the contact and signs it in. |
| No `userHash`, verification not required, existing email | The app does not update or sign in the contact. `data-pilgrim-link` opens `/posts` without a sign-in. |

The widget never signs in the admin contact of a user. For an admin contact, `data-pilgrim-link` opens `/posts` without a sign-in.

**Require identity verification** is in **Settings > Embed Widget**. It is on for a new project. It is off for a project that existed before the setting. Turn it on after your app sends `userHash`.

## Release notes

If `releaseNotes.show` is `true`, the widget adds a hidden iframe with the release notes of the project. A click on an element with `data-pilgrim-release-notes` shows the iframe.

If `releaseNotes.open` is also `true`, the widget opens the iframe two seconds after the page loads. It does this only when the contact has not seen the newest note yet. The app stores the last note that it opened for each contact. Without a valid `userHash` for an existing contact, the iframe does not open by itself.

## Testimonials

If `testimonials` is `true`, the widget adds a hidden iframe with the testimonial form. A click on an element with `data-pilgrim-testimonials` shows the iframe.

When the app knows the contact, the iframe URL holds a signed contact token that stays valid for 24 hours. The testimonial then belongs to the contact. Without a valid token, the testimonial is from `Anonymous User`. Read [Testimonials](testimonials.md).

## Errors

| Status | Body | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | `{"error": "Invalid client key"}` | The key is not the publishable key of a project, or every user of the project is deactivated. |
| `403` | `{"error": "Identity verification failed"}` | Read [Identity verification](#identity-verification). |
| `422` | `{"message": "...", "errors": {...}}` or `{"error": "The request must include a contact with an email."}` | The request has no contact email. |

## The internal widget endpoints

The widget and its iframes use these endpoints. They are not part of the versioned REST API.

| Method | Path | Host | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/init` | Any | Signs in the contact and returns the iframe URLs. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/release-notes` | The public site | Lists the release notes with a publication date. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/testimonials/settings` | The public site | Returns `{"rating_enabled": true}` or `false`. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/testimonials` | The public site | Stores a testimonial from the iframe. 5 requests a minute for each IP address. |
| `GET` | `/iframe/release-notes` | The public site | The release notes iframe. |
| `GET` | `/iframe/testimonials` | The public site | The testimonial form iframe. |
| `GET` | `/iframe/roadmap` | The public site | The roadmap iframe. |

The iframes and the page talk with `postMessage`. The iframe routes send `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/webhooks-and-slack.md

# Webhooks and Slack

A project can send events to your own server with webhooks, and messages to a Slack channel. The queue worker sends both. Read [Queues and the scheduler](../self-hosting/queues-and-scheduler.md).

## Webhooks

Open **Settings > Webhooks**. A webhook has:

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| URL | Required. An `https` URL with 2048 characters or fewer. The host must resolve to a public IP address. The URL cannot contain a user name or a password. |
| Events | One or more of the events below. |
| Active | On or off. A paused webhook gets no events. |

The app makes a signing secret of 40 characters for each webhook. The settings page shows the secret.

### Events

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `post.created` | The app creates a post, from any source: the public site, the dashboard, the REST API or the MCP server. |
| `post.status_changed` | A user moves a post to another stage in the dashboard. |
| `post.completed` | A user moves a post to a `complete` stage in the dashboard, and the post was not complete before. |

A move to a `complete` stage sends both `post.status_changed` and `post.completed`. A status change from the REST API or the MCP server sends the same events.

### The request

The app sends a `POST` request with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "event": "post.status_changed",
  "data": {
    "id": 42,
    "title": "Add dark mode",
    "content": "Users want a dark theme.",
    "status": "in_progress",
    "board_id": 1,
    "contact_id": 7,
    "stage": {
      "id": 4,
      "name": "In Progress",
      "type": "active"
    }
  }
}
```

The request has these headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Event` | The event, for example `post.created` |
| `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Delivery` | The ID of the delivery, a UUID. Each retry of the same delivery sends the same ID. |
| `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Timestamp` | The Unix time of the try, in seconds. Each retry sends a new time. |
| `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature-V2` | The HMAC-SHA256 of `<timestamp>.<raw body>`, with the signing secret as the key, in hexadecimal |
| `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature` | Deprecated. The HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body only. The next release removes it. |

### Verify the signature

1. Join the value of `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Timestamp`, a `.` and the raw body.
2. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of this string with your signing secret.
3. Compare the result with `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature-V2`. Use a comparison in constant time.
4. If the timestamp is more than 5 minutes from the current time, reject the request.
5. If you already handled the delivery ID, ignore the request.

In a Laravel app:

```php
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;

Route::post('/feedback-pilgrim/webhook', function (Request $request) {
    $timestamp = (string) $request->header('X-FeedbackPilgrim-Timestamp');
    $expected = hash_hmac('sha256', $timestamp.'.'.$request->getContent(), config('services.feedback_pilgrim.webhook_secret'));

    abort_unless(hash_equals($expected, (string) $request->header('X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature-V2')), 401);
    abort_if(abs(time() - (int) $timestamp) > 300, 401);

    if (! Cache::add('feedback-pilgrim:'.$request->header('X-FeedbackPilgrim-Delivery'), true, now()->addDay())) {
        return response()->noContent();
    }

    $event = $request->input('event');
    $post = $request->input('data');

    // Handle the event.

    return response()->noContent();
});
```

Use the raw body. If you encode the parsed JSON again, the signature can be different.

The old `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature` header signs the body only, so it cannot stop a replayed request. If your receiver reads it, change the receiver to `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature-V2` before the next release.

### Retries and the delivery log

If your server answers with a `4xx` or `5xx` status, or if the connection fails, the app tries again. The app tries three times in total. It waits 10 seconds, then 60 seconds, between the tries.

The app logs each try: the event, the status code and the result. The app does not store the response body. The result is one of these values:

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `delivered` | Your server answered with a `2xx` status. |
| `http_error` | Your server answered with a `4xx` or `5xx` status. |
| `redirect_refused` | Your server answered with a redirect. The app does not follow redirects. |
| `connection_failed` | The app could not connect, or the request timed out. |
| `address_refused` | The host of the URL resolved to an address that is not public. The app did not send the request and does not try again. |

The settings page shows the five newest tries for each webhook.

## Slack

1. In Slack, create an incoming webhook for a channel. Copy its URL.
2. In the dashboard, open **Settings > Integrations**.
3. Paste the URL in the Slack field. The URL must start with `https://hooks.slack.com/`.
4. Save.

To stop the messages, clear the field and save.

The app posts these messages:

| When | Message |
|---|---|
| The app creates a post | `🆕 New feedback: *<title>*` and the link of the post |
| A post moves to another stage, from the dashboard, the REST API or the MCP server | `🔄 *<title>* moved to *<stage>*` and the link of the post |

If Slack answers with a `4xx` or `5xx` status, the app tries again. It tries three times in total.

The app makes the link with the host of the request that caused the message. A post from the public site gets a link on the public site. A stage change in the dashboard gets a link on the dashboard host.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/using-feedback-pilgrim/admin-area.md

# The admin area

The admin area is at `/admin` on the dashboard host. Only an owner can open it. For other users and for guests, each admin page returns 404. An owner sees the **Admin** link in the sidebar.

Read [Accounts and registration](../self-hosting/accounts-and-registration.md) to make a user an owner.

## Users

Open **Admin > Users** (`/admin/users`). The list shows all the users of the instance, the newest first, 25 on each page. Each row shows the projects of the user. You can search by name or email.

### Deactivate a user

Click **Deactivate** on the row of the user. A deactivated user keeps all their data, but cannot authenticate:

- The login form refuses the user and shows the reason.
- An open web session ends at the next request. A "Remember me" cookie stops working.
- The API tokens of the user stop working. This includes the MCP server.
- The sign-in link of the admin contact of the user returns 404 on the public site.

A project keeps its public site, its iframes and its widget while one of its users is active. When every user of a project is deactivated, these stop too, and the widget gets 401.

To restore access, click **Reactivate**. The tokens of the user work again.

The owner cannot deactivate an owner. The app returns 403 with `You cannot deactivate an owner.`

## Settings

Open **Admin > Settings** (`/admin/settings`). The page has one setting: the registration mode.

| Mode | Effect |
|---|---|
| Closed | Nobody can sign up. `/register` returns 404. |
| Open | Anyone can sign up and create projects. |

The mode that the owner saves stays in the database. It wins over `REGISTRATION_ENABLED`. Read [Accounts and registration](../self-hosting/accounts-and-registration.md).

## Commands for the owner

The owner can also manage users in the terminal:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `php artisan fp:user:list` | Lists the users, with their projects, owner flag and status. |
| `php artisan fp:user:password` | Sets a new password for a user. |
| `php artisan fp:install --promote=<email>` | Makes an existing user an owner. |

Read [Recover access](../self-hosting/recover-access.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/api/overview.md

# API overview

The REST API reads and writes the data of one project: posts, release notes, contacts, testimonials and tags. Each request uses an API token, and the token decides the project. Read [Authentication](authentication.md).

The OpenAPI spec and the Postman collection describe each endpoint. Read [OpenAPI and Postman](openapi.md).

The MCP server uses the same code and the same validation. Read [MCP server](../mcp/overview.md).

## Base URL

```text
https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1
```

Use the dashboard host of your instance, that is the host of `APP_URL`.

## Keys

The API uses two keys:

| Key | Where to get it | Endpoints |
|---|---|---|
| API token | **Settings > API Tokens**. Read [Authentication](authentication.md). | All endpoints of `/api/public/v1` |
| Publishable key (`pk_`) | **Settings > Embed Widget**. Read [Widget init](widget.md). | `POST /api/v1/init` only |

An API token has all abilities (`*`) and no expiry date. The app has no token abilities to limit a token. A token can read and change all the data of its project.

The publishable key is public. The widget sends it from the browser. It gives no access to the REST API.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/init` | [Init](init.md) |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/posts` | [Posts](posts.md) |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/posts/{id}` | [Posts](posts.md) |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/release-notes` | [Release notes](release-notes.md) |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/release-notes/{id}` | [Release notes](release-notes.md) |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/contacts` | [Contacts](contacts.md) |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH` | `/contacts/{id}` | [Contacts](contacts.md) |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/testimonials` | [Testimonials](testimonials.md) |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/testimonials/{id}` | [Testimonials](testimonials.md) |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/tags` | [Tags](tags.md) |
| `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/tags/{id}` | [Tags](tags.md) |

The widget endpoint has another prefix and another key:

| Method | Path | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/init` | [Widget init](widget.md) |

An update accepts `PUT` or `PATCH`. Both change only the fields that you send.

`DELETE` on a post, a release note or a testimonial always returns `405` with `{"message": "Method not allowed"}`. The only delete in the API is the delete of a tag.

## Request format

Send these headers with each request:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
```

Send `Accept: application/json`. Without it, an error can come back as a redirect instead of JSON.

The app does not read a project ID from the request. It takes the project from the token. A record of another project returns `404`.

## Lists and pagination

Each list endpoint accepts these query parameters:

| Parameter | Default | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | `1` | A number below 1 counts as 1. |
| `per_page` | `15` | Maximum 100. A number below 1 counts as 15. |
| `search` | none | Finds the text in some fields. Each endpoint page lists the fields. |
| `sort_by` | Differs for each endpoint | One of the columns that the endpoint page lists. |
| `sort_direction` | `desc` (`asc` for tags) | `asc` or `desc`. Another value counts as the default. |

If `sort_by` is not in the list of the endpoint, the list has no fixed order. The tags list is different: it sorts by `title`.

A list returns the pagination object of Laravel:

```json
{
  "current_page": 1,
  "data": [],
  "first_page_url": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts?page=1",
  "from": 1,
  "last_page": 3,
  "last_page_url": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts?page=3",
  "links": [],
  "next_page_url": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts?page=2",
  "path": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts",
  "per_page": 15,
  "prev_page_url": null,
  "to": 15,
  "total": 42
}
```

The records are in `data`. To read all the pages, follow `next_page_url` until it is `null`.

## Errors

| Status | Body | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | `{"message": "Unauthenticated."}` | The token is missing, wrong or deleted, or its user is deactivated. |
| `401` | `{"error": "Invalid API token"}` | The token has no project, or its user is not a member of the project now. |
| `404` | `{"message": "..."}` | The record does not exist in the project of the token. |
| `405` | `{"message": "Method not allowed"}` | A delete that the API does not support. |
| `422` | `{"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}` | The request failed validation. |
| `429` | `{"message": "Too Many Attempts."}` | The rate limit stopped the request. |

A `422` body looks like this:

```json
{
  "message": "The title field is required.",
  "errors": {
    "title": ["The title field is required."]
  }
}
```

## Rate limit

The API allows 120 requests a minute for each user. All the tokens of one user share this limit. Without a user, for example for the widget init call, the limit applies to each IP address.

Each response has the headers `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. A `429` response also has `Retry-After`, the number of seconds to wait. The MCP server has its own limit. Read [MCP server](../mcp/overview.md#rate-limit).

## Dates

The API returns dates as ISO 8601 strings in UTC, for example `2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/api/authentication.md

# Authentication

The REST API and the MCP server accept an API token. An API token is a Laravel Sanctum personal access token. Each token belongs to one user and one project.

## Make a token

1. In the dashboard, choose the project in the project selector.
2. Open **Settings > API Tokens**.
3. Click **Generate token**.
4. Copy the token. The page shows it one time only.

The token belongs to the project that is active when you click the button. The token has all abilities (`*`) and no expiry date. The app gives each token the name `API Key`.

The token has the form `<id>|<random characters>`. Send the full value.

## Send the token

Send the token in the `Authorization` header:

```bash
curl https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/tags \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

In PHP with the Laravel HTTP client:

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

$api = Http::withToken(config('services.feedback_pilgrim.token'))
    ->acceptJson()
    ->baseUrl('https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1');

$tags = $api->get('/tags')->throw()->json('data');
```

Keep the token in the configuration of your server, for example in `.env`. The examples in these docs read it with `config('services.feedback_pilgrim.token')`.

WARNING: Never put an API token in HTML or in browser JavaScript. The token can read and change all the data of the project. For the browser, use the publishable key of the widget. Read [The embeddable widget](../using-feedback-pilgrim/widget.md).

## When a token stops working

A token works only while all these conditions are true:

- The token exists.
- The user of the token is not deactivated.
- The user of the token is still a member of the project of the token.

If the owner deactivates the user, the token returns `401`. If the owner reactivates the user, the token works again.

## Delete a token

1. Open **Settings > API Tokens**.
2. Find the token in **Active tokens**. Each row shows the date of creation and the last use.
3. Click **Delete**.

The page lists the tokens of the active project only.

## The MCP server

The MCP server at `/mcp` accepts the same token. Read [Connect a client](../mcp/connecting-clients.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/api/init.md

# Init

`POST /init` creates or updates a contact and returns a sign-in link for the public site. Call it from your server, for example to add a "Feedback" link to a page of your app.

This endpoint uses an API token. The widget uses a different endpoint, `/api/v1/init`, with the publishable key. Read [The embeddable widget](../using-feedback-pilgrim/widget.md).

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/init` | Creates or updates a contact, and returns `auth_url`. |

## Request

```http
POST /api/public/v1/init
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contact` | object | No | The contact. It needs `email` to create or update a contact. |
| `contact.email` | string | With `contact` | The email of the contact. The app finds the contact by email in the project. |
| `contact.name` | string | No | The name. |
| `contact.mrr` | number | No | The monthly recurring revenue. |
| `contact.ltv` | number | No | The lifetime value. |
| `contact.avatar` | string | No | The URL of an avatar image. |
| `contact.<other>` | any | No | A custom attribute. The app ignores `top_customer`. |

You can also send the contact nested as `contact.contact`. The app reads the email from `contact.email` or `contact.contact.email`.

The endpoint does not check an identity hash. The API token proves that the request comes from your server.

## Response

`200` with the sign-in link, if the request had a contact email:

```json
{
  "auth_url": "https://acme.feedback.example.com/authenticate/9b1c...?expires=1763463600&signature=..."
}
```

`200` with an empty JSON array (`[]`), if the request had no contact email.

The link signs in the contact on the public site of the project. It stays valid for 24 hours. Make a new link for each page view. Do not store it.

Each call also counts a session for the contact, one a day at most.

## Examples

```bash
curl -X POST https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/init \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"contact":{"email":"jane@example.com","name":"Jane Doe","mrr":49,"plan":"pro"}}'
```

In PHP, redirect the signed-in user of your app to the public site:

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

$authUrl = Http::withToken(config('services.feedback_pilgrim.token'))
    ->acceptJson()
    ->post('https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/init', [
        'contact' => [
            'email' => $user->email,
            'name' => $user->name,
            'mrr' => $user->monthly_revenue,
        ],
    ])
    ->throw()
    ->json('auth_url');

return redirect()->away($authUrl);
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/api/posts.md

# Posts

A post is one piece of feedback. Read [Posts, votes and comments](../using-feedback-pilgrim/posts-votes-and-comments.md) for the concepts.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/posts` | Lists the posts. |
| `POST` | `/posts` | Creates a post. |
| `GET` | `/posts/{id}` | Returns one post. |
| `PUT`, `PATCH` | `/posts/{id}` | Updates a post. |
| `DELETE` | `/posts/{id}` | Not supported. Returns `405`. |

## The post object

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "client_id": 1,
  "stage_id": 4,
  "board_id": 1,
  "contact_id": 7,
  "title": "Add dark mode",
  "content": "Users want a dark theme.",
  "notes": null,
  "status": "in_progress",
  "stage_position": null,
  "published_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "archived_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "contact": {"id": 7, "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com"},
  "tags": [{"id": 3, "client_id": 1, "title": "ui"}],
  "votes": [{"id": 90, "contact_id": 7}]
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `client_id` | The ID of the project. |
| `stage_id` | The stage of the post. |
| `status` | `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`. The app derives it from the stage. Read [Stages and the roadmap](../using-feedback-pilgrim/stages-and-roadmap.md#stage-types-and-the-status-of-a-post). |
| `notes` | The private notes of the team. |
| `published_at` | The publication date. If `null`, the public site does not show the post. |
| `archived_at` | The archive date, or `null`. |
| `contact` | The author, or `null`. |

The list adds `contact`, `tags` and `votes` to each post. One post also has `comments`. Create and update return `tags` and `contact`. Create also returns `stage`.

A `contact` inside a post has the custom attributes as one JSON string in `metadata`.

## List posts

```http
GET /posts
```

| Parameter | In | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `page`, `per_page` | query | Pagination. Read [API overview](overview.md#lists-and-pagination). |
| `search` | query | Finds the text in `title` or `content`. |
| `status` | query | `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`. |
| `board_id` | query | Only the posts of this board. |
| `tag` | query | Only the posts with a tag of this title. |
| `published` | query | `true` for published posts only, `false` for unpublished posts only. |
| `sort_by` | query | `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `title`, `status` or `published_at`. |
| `sort_direction` | query | `desc` (default) or `asc`. |

### Example request

```bash
curl 'https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts?status=pending&per_page=50' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example response

`200`:

```json
{
  "current_page": 1,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 42,
      "client_id": 1,
      "stage_id": 1,
      "board_id": 1,
      "contact_id": 7,
      "title": "Add dark mode",
      "content": "Users want a dark theme.",
      "notes": null,
```

## Get a post

```http
GET /posts/{id}
```

Returns the post with `contact`, `tags`, `votes` and `comments`. `404` means that the post is not in the project of the token.

### Example request

```bash
curl https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts/42 \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Create a post

```http
POST /posts
```

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | Maximum 255 characters |
| `content` | string | Yes | |
| `status` | string | No | `pending` (default), `in_progress` or `completed` |
| `board_id` | integer | No | A board of the project. Default: the first board. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs of the project |

`201` returns the new post.

A post from the API has no author and is not published. Publish it in the dashboard. The app sends the `post.created` webhook event and the Slack message.

CAUTION: Do not repeat a failed create request without a check. Each request creates a new post.

### Example request

```bash
curl -X POST https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Add dark mode","content":"Users want a dark theme.","tags":[3]}'
```

### Example response

`201`:

```json
{
  "title": "Add dark mode",
  "content": "Users want a dark theme.",
  "status": "pending",
  "board_id": 1,
  "client_id": 1,
  "stage_id": 1,
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "id": 43,
  "stage": {
    "id": 1,
    "client_id": 1,
    "name": "Open",
    "position": 1,
    "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
    "slug": "open",
    "color": "#94a3b8",
    "type": "open",
    "show_on_roadmap": false
  },
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "client_id": 1,
      "title": "ui",
      "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z"
    }
  ],
  "contact": null
}
```

## Update a post

```http
PATCH /posts/{id}
```

Send only the fields to change.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Maximum 255 characters |
| `content` | string | |
| `status` | string | `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed` |
| `board_id` | integer | A board of the project |
| `tags` | integer array | Tag IDs of the project. The list replaces all the tags of the post. |

`200` returns the post.

A new `status` moves the post to the first stage of the matching type. The app then sends the same emails, webhook events and Slack message as a stage change in the dashboard. Read [Stages and the roadmap](../using-feedback-pilgrim/stages-and-roadmap.md). If the status does not change, the app sends nothing.

### Example request

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts/42 \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"status":"in_progress"}'
```

### Example response

`200`:

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "client_id": 1,
  "stage_id": 4,
  "board_id": 1,
  "contact_id": 7,
  "title": "Add dark mode",
  "content": "Users want a dark theme.",
  "notes": null,
  "status": "in_progress",
  "stage_position": null,
  "published_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "archived_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "client_id": 1,
      "title": "ui",
      "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z"
    }
  ],
  "contact": {
    "id": 7,
    "uuid": "4f6c2a5e-7d3b-4d1e-9c8a-2b1f0e9d8c7b",
    "user_id": null,
    "client_id": 1,
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "metadata": "{\"plan\":\"pro\"}",
    "notes": null,
    "avatar": "https://feedback.example.com/storage/avatars/7/avatar.png",
    "mrr": 49,
    "ltv": 1200,
    "top_customer": 0,
    "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z"
  }
}
```

## Delete a post

```http
DELETE /posts/{id}
```

The API cannot delete a post.

### Example request

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/posts/42 \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example response

`405`:

```json
{
  "message": "Method not allowed"
}
```

## PHP example

Create a post, then read all the pending posts, in PHP:

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

$api = Http::withToken(config('services.feedback_pilgrim.token'))
    ->acceptJson()
    ->baseUrl('https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1');

$post = $api->post('/posts', [
    'title' => 'Add dark mode',
    'content' => 'Users want a dark theme.',
])->throw()->json();

$pending = [];
$page = 1;

do {
    $response = $api->get('/posts', ['status' => 'pending', 'page' => $page, 'per_page' => 100])->throw();
    $pending = array_merge($pending, $response->json('data'));
    $page++;
} while ($response->json('next_page_url') !== null);
```

# Release notes

A release note is a changelog entry of a project. Read [Release notes](../using-feedback-pilgrim/release-notes.md) for the concepts.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/release-notes` | Lists the release notes. |
| `POST` | `/release-notes` | Creates a release note. |
| `GET` | `/release-notes/{id}` | Returns one release note. |
| `PUT`, `PATCH` | `/release-notes/{id}` | Updates a release note. |
| `DELETE` | `/release-notes/{id}` | Not supported. Returns `405`. |

## The release note object

```json
{
  "id": 7,
  "client_id": 1,
  "user_id": 1,
  "title": "New dashboard",
  "content": "The dashboard has a new layout.",
  "slug": "new-dashboard-20261117",
  "published_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "tags": [],
  "votes": [],
  "comments": []
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `user_id` | The user who wrote the note. For a note from the API, the user of the token. |
| `slug` | The path of the note on the public site: `/release-notes/<slug>`. |
| `published_at` | The publication date. `null` means that the note is a draft. The public site shows only notes with a publication date. |

The list and one note add `tags`, `votes` and `comments`. Create and update return `tags`.

## List release notes

```http
GET /release-notes
```

| Parameter | In | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `page`, `per_page` | query | Pagination. Read [API overview](overview.md#lists-and-pagination). |
| `search` | query | Finds the text in `title` or `content`. |
| `published` | query | `true` for notes with a publication date, `false` for notes without one. |
| `tag` | query | Only the notes with a tag of this title. |
| `sort_by` | query | `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `title` or `published_at`. |
| `sort_direction` | query | `desc` (default) or `asc`. |

### Example request

```bash
curl 'https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/release-notes?published=false' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-token>' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example response

`200`:

```json
{
  "current_page": 1,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 7,
      "client_id": 1,
      "user_id": 1,
      "title": "New dashboard",
      "content": "The dashboard has a new layout.",
      "slug": "new-dashboard-20261117",
      "published_at": null,
      "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
      "tags": [
        {
          "id": 3,
          "client_id": 1,
          "title": "ui",
          "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
          "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z"
        }
      ],
      "votes": [],
      "comments": []
    }
  ],
  "first_page_url": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/release-notes?page=1",
  "from": 1,
  "last_page": 1,
  "last_page_url": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/release-notes?page=1",
  "links": [],
  "next_page_url": null,
  "path": "https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/release-notes",
  "per_page": 15,
  "prev_page_url": null,
  "to": 1,
  "total": 1
}
```

## Get a release note

```http
GET /release-notes/{id}
```

Returns the note with `tags`, `votes` and `comments`.

### Example request

```bash
curl https://feedback.example.com/api/public/v1/release-notes/7 \

  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

```json
{
  "id": 7,
  "client_id": 1,
  "user_id": 1,
  "title": "New dashboard",
  "content": "The dashboard has a new layout.",
  "slug": "new-dashboard-20261117",
  "published_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:00:00.000000Z",
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 3,
```
