Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/mcp/overview.md

# MCP server

Each instance has a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. An AI agent can use it to read and change the data of one project: posts, release notes, contacts, testimonials and tags.

The MCP server and the REST API use the same code and the same validation. Read [API overview](../api/overview.md).

## The endpoint

```text
https://feedback.example.com/mcp
```

The endpoint is on the dashboard host, that is the host of `APP_URL`. The **Settings > API Tokens** page of the dashboard shows the URL.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Server name | `Feedback Pilgrim` |
| Server version | `1.0.0` |
| Tools | 21. Read [MCP tools reference](tools-reference.md). |
| State | Stateless |

The **Settings > API Tokens** page shows the badge "20 tools". The server registers 21 tools.

## Authentication

The server accepts an API token as a bearer token only:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>
```

Make the token in **Settings > API Tokens**. Read [Authentication](../api/authentication.md).

- The token decides the project. A tool never takes a project ID.
- The server refuses a session cookie. A request without a valid token gets `401`.
- If the owner deactivates the user of the token, the token stops working.

## Rate limit

The server allows 60 requests a minute for each token. This limit is separate from the limit of the REST API.

## Responses

A list tool returns an object with `records` and `pagination`:

```json
{
  "records": [
    {"id": 42, "title": "Add dark mode", "status": "pending"}
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 15,
    "total": 42,
    "has_more": true
  }
}
```

To get the next page, call the tool again with `page` plus one. Stop when `has_more` is `false`.

A get, create or update tool returns the record as JSON. The fields are the same as in the REST API.

## Errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| The record is not in the project of the token | A tool error with the text `Resource not found.` |
| The arguments fail validation | A tool error with the validation messages |
| No token, a wrong token, or a deactivated user | HTTP `401` |
| More than 60 requests a minute | HTTP `429` |

## Write tools

These tools change data: `create_post`, `update_post`, `create_post_comment`, `create_release_note`, `update_release_note`, `create_contact`, `update_contact`, `create_testimonial`, `update_testimonial`, `create_tag`, `update_tag` and `delete_tag`.

CAUTION: Do not let an agent repeat a failed create call without a check. Each call of a create tool makes a new record. `create_contact` is the exception: it updates the contact with the same email.

`create_post_comment` sends an email to the author of the post. The comment comes from the admin contact of the user of the token.

## Next steps

- [Connect a client](connecting-clients.md)
- [MCP tools reference](tools-reference.md)

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/mcp/connecting-clients.md

# Connect a client

The **Settings > API Tokens** page of the dashboard shows a snippet for each client. Paste a token in the **Auth token** field of the page, and the snippets fill in the token.

Before you start:

1. Make an API token for the project. Read [Authentication](../api/authentication.md).
2. Copy the server URL from **Settings > API Tokens**, for example `https://feedback.example.com/mcp`.

After you change the configuration of a client, restart the client.

On the server, `fp:mcp:connect` prints the configuration for each client. With `--token=new`, it also makes a token with the abilities `mcp:read` and `mcp:write`:

```bash
docker exec feedbackpilgrim php artisan fp:mcp:connect --client=claude --token=new
```

`--client` accepts `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` and `json`. The printed lines read the token from the `FP_TOKEN` environment variable, so the token is not in your shell history.

## The instance-admin server

A second MCP server operates the instance: status, doctor, users, projects, API tokens, the queue and a test email. It uses stdio over SSH and `docker exec`. It needs no token and no open port:

```bash
claude mcp add fp-admin -- ssh <host> docker exec -i feedbackpilgrim php artisan mcp:start fp-admin
```

A destructive tool returns a preview first, and changes data only after a second call with `confirm: true`. The server writes each call to the `mcp-admin` log. An HTTP route at `/mcp/admin` exists only when `MCP_ADMIN_ENABLED=true`. It accepts only short-lived owner tokens from `fp:token:create --admin`.

## Claude Code

Run these commands in your terminal:

```bash
export FP_TOKEN=<your-token>
claude mcp add --transport http feedback-pilgrim https://feedback.example.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${FP_TOKEN}"
```

## Claude Desktop

Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "feedback-pilgrim": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://feedback.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Codex

Run these commands in your terminal:

```bash
export FP_TOKEN=<your-token>
codex mcp add feedback-pilgrim --url https://feedback.example.com/mcp --bearer-token-env-var FP_TOKEN
```

An older Codex without `--url` connects through `mcp-remote`. Add the server to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.feedback-pilgrim]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://feedback.example.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"]
```

## Cursor and other clients

Add the server to the `mcp.json` file of the client, for example `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "feedback-pilgrim": {
      "url": "https://feedback.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A client must send the token in the `Authorization` header. The server does not support OAuth.

## Test the connection

Ask the agent to list the tags of the project. The agent calls `list_tags`. If the answer is an error about authentication, read the next section.

## If the connection fails

- If the client gets `401`, make sure that the token is complete, with the part before the `|`.
- If the client gets `401` with a correct token, make sure that the user of the token is active. The user must also be a member of the project.
- If the client gets `429`, the client sent more than 60 requests in a minute.
- If the client cannot reach the server, open `https://feedback.example.com/up` in a browser. The page must load.

## More than one project

A token belongs to one project. To use two projects:

1. Make a token in each project.
2. Add the server one time for each token.
3. Give each server a different name, for example `feedback-pilgrim-acme` and `feedback-pilgrim-beta`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/mcp/tools-reference.md

# MCP tools reference

The Feedback Pilgrim MCP server has 21 tools. This page lists them in the order that `tools/list` returns them. The source is the tool classes in `app/Mcp/Tools` of the app. If a tool changes, update this page.

Each tool works on the project of the token. No tool takes a project ID. A record of another project gives the error `Resource not found.`

The list tools share these arguments:

| Argument | Type | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | 1 or more | The page to return. Default 1. |
| `per_page` | integer | 1 to 100 | The records on each page. Default 15. |
| `sort_direction` | string | `asc` or `desc` | The sort direction. |

Read [MCP server](overview.md) for the response format.

## Summary

| Tool | What it does | Changes data |
|---|---|---|
| [`list_posts`](#list_posts) | Lists the posts. | No |
| [`get_post`](#get_post) | Returns one post. | No |
| [`create_post`](#create_post) | Creates a post. | Yes |
| [`update_post`](#update_post) | Updates a post. | Yes |
| [`create_post_comment`](#create_post_comment) | Replies to a post. | Yes |
| [`list_release_notes`](#list_release_notes) | Lists the release notes. | No |
| [`get_release_note`](#get_release_note) | Returns one release note. | No |
| [`create_release_note`](#create_release_note) | Creates a release note. | Yes |
| [`update_release_note`](#update_release_note) | Updates a release note. | Yes |
| [`list_contacts`](#list_contacts) | Lists the contacts. | No |
| [`get_contact`](#get_contact) | Returns one contact. | No |
| [`create_contact`](#create_contact) | Creates or updates a contact by email. | Yes |
| [`update_contact`](#update_contact) | Updates a contact. | Yes |
| [`list_testimonials`](#list_testimonials) | Lists the testimonials. | No |
| [`get_testimonial`](#get_testimonial) | Returns one testimonial. | No |
| [`create_testimonial`](#create_testimonial) | Creates a testimonial. | Yes |
| [`update_testimonial`](#update_testimonial) | Updates or approves a testimonial. | Yes |
| [`list_tags`](#list_tags) | Lists the tags. | No |
| [`create_tag`](#create_tag) | Creates a tag. | Yes |
| [`update_tag`](#update_tag) | Renames a tag. | Yes |
| [`delete_tag`](#delete_tag) | Deletes a tag. | Yes |

## list_posts

Lists the posts of the project. Each post has its contact, tags and votes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | No | The page. |
| `per_page` | integer | No | The records on each page, maximum 100. |
| `search` | string | No | Finds the text in the title or the content. |
| `status` | string | No | `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`. |
| `tag` | string | No | Only the posts with a tag of this title. |
| `published` | boolean | No | `true` for published posts only, `false` for unpublished posts only. |
| `sort_by` | string | No | `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `title`, `status` or `published_at`. |
| `sort_direction` | string | No | `asc` or `desc` (default). |

## get_post

Returns one post with its contact, tags, votes and comments.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the post. |

## create_post

Creates a post. The post has no author and is not published. Each call makes a new post.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | The title, 255 characters or fewer. |
| `content` | string | Yes | The text of the post. |
| `status` | string | No | `pending` (default), `in_progress` or `completed`. |
| `board_id` | integer | No | A board of the project. Default: the first board. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs of the project. |

The result is the post with its tags and contact.

## update_post

Updates a post. Only the arguments that you send change. A new `status` moves the post to the first stage of the matching type. The app then sends the same emails, webhook events and Slack message as a stage change in the dashboard.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the post. |
| `title` | string | No | The new title. |
| `content` | string | No | The new text. |
| `status` | string | No | `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`. |
| `board_id` | integer | No | Moves the post to this board of the project. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs. The list replaces all the tags of the post. |

## create_post_comment

Replies to a post. The comment comes from the admin contact of the user of the token. If the post has an author, the author gets an email. Each call adds a new comment.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `post_id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the post. |
| `content` | string | Yes | The text of the comment. |

The result is the comment with its contact.

## list_release_notes

Lists the release notes of the project. Each note has its tags, votes and comments.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | No | The page. |
| `per_page` | integer | No | The records on each page, maximum 100. |
| `search` | string | No | Finds the text in the title or the content. |
| `published` | boolean | No | `true` for notes with a publication date, `false` for notes without one. |
| `tag` | string | No | Only the notes with a tag of this title. |
| `sort_by` | string | No | `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `title` or `published_at`. |
| `sort_direction` | string | No | `asc` or `desc` (default). |

## get_release_note

Returns one release note with its tags, votes and comments.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the release note. |

## create_release_note

Creates a release note. Without `published: true`, the note is a draft with no publication date. The user of the token is the author. Each call makes a new note.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Yes | The title, 255 characters or fewer. |
| `content` | string | Yes | The text. Markdown is allowed. |
| `published` | boolean | No | `true` publishes the note with the current time as the publication date. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs of the project. |

## update_release_note

Updates a release note. Only the arguments that you send change.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the release note. |
| `title` | string | No | The new title. |
| `content` | string | No | The new text. |
| `published` | boolean | No | `true` publishes the note and keeps a publication date that exists. `false` clears the publication date. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs. The list replaces all the tags of the note. |

## list_contacts

Lists the contacts of the project. Each contact has its tags and votes. The custom attributes are fields of each record.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | No | The page. |
| `per_page` | integer | No | The records on each page, maximum 100. |
| `search` | string | No | Finds the text in the name or the email. |
| `tag` | string | No | Only the contacts with a tag of this title. |
| `sort_by` | string | No | `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `name`, `email`, `mrr` or `ltv`. |
| `sort_direction` | string | No | `asc` or `desc` (default). |

## get_contact

Returns one contact with its tags and votes. The custom attributes are fields of the record.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the contact. |

## create_contact

Creates a contact, or updates the contact with the same email in the project. The result has the field `was_created`: `true` for a new contact, `false` for an update.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Yes | The name, 255 characters or fewer. |
| `email` | string | Yes | The email. The tool finds the contact by this value. |
| `avatar` | string | No | The URL of an avatar image. |
| `mrr` | number | No | The monthly recurring revenue. |
| `ltv` | number | No | The lifetime value. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs of the project. |

Other arguments become custom attributes, with the limits in [Contacts](../api/contacts.md#create-or-update-a-contact).

## update_contact

Updates a contact. Only the arguments that you send change.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the contact. |
| `name` | string | No | The new name. |
| `email` | string | No | The new email. It must be unique in the project. |
| `avatar` | string | No | The new avatar URL. |
| `mrr` | number | No | The monthly recurring revenue. |
| `ltv` | number | No | The lifetime value. |
| `tags` | integer array | No | Tag IDs. The list replaces all the tags of the contact. |

## list_testimonials

Lists the testimonials of the project. Each testimonial has its contact, votes and comments.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `search` | string | No | Finds the text in the description or the user name. |
| `approved` | boolean | No | `true` for the approved testimonials. If you omit it, or send `false`, the list holds the pending testimonials only. |
| `rating` | integer | No | Only the testimonials with this rating, 1 to 5. |

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Yes | The ID of the tag. |

CAUTION: You cannot undo a delete. This is the only delete tool of the server.

# Reverse proxy and TLS

The container gets its own TLS certificates by default. You need your own proxy only if another web server already uses ports 80 and 443, or if Cloudflare or a load balancer is in front of the server.

## DNS

Make two DNS records that point to your server:

| Record | Example | What it serves |
|---|---|---|
| The dashboard domain | `feedback.example.com` | The dashboard, the REST API, the MCP server and `pilgrim.js` |
| A wildcard for the projects | `*.feedback.example.com` | The public site of each project |

## Automatic HTTPS

When `APP_DOMAIN` is set, Caddy in the container serves ports 80 and 443. Publish both ports:

```bash
docker run -d --name feedbackpilgrim --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 80:80 -p 443:443 -p 443:443/udp \
  -e APP_DOMAIN=feedback.example.com \
  -v feedbackpilgrim:/data \
  ghcr.io/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim
```

Caddy uses on-demand TLS. It gets a certificate from Let's Encrypt for each host on the first visit. Before it asks for a certificate, Caddy asks the app if the host is the dashboard domain or the subdomain of a project. Caddy gets no certificate for other hosts.

- You need no wildcard certificate and no DNS API key.
- The certificates stay in the `/data` volume.
- Port 80 must be open. Let's Encrypt checks the host on port 80, and Caddy redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
- The first visit to a new project subdomain takes one or two seconds more while Caddy gets the certificate.
- To get notices from Let's Encrypt about the certificates, set `ACME_EMAIL`.

## Your own proxy

To use your own proxy, set `CADDY_ENABLED=false` and publish only port 8080 of the container:

```bash
docker run -d --name feedbackpilgrim --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  -e APP_DOMAIN=feedback.example.com \
  -e CADDY_ENABLED=false \
  -e TRUSTED_PROXIES=172.16.0.0/12 \
  -v feedbackpilgrim:/data \
  ghcr.io/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim
```

Port 8080 serves plain HTTP. The proxy must serve HTTPS, with a certificate that covers the dashboard domain and the wildcard. Most ACME clients need a DNS challenge for a wildcard certificate.

## Send the traffic to the app

Send both names to port 8080 of the container. Keep the original `Host` header, because the app finds the project from the host.

The [`deploy/`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/tree/main/deploy) folder of the app repository has an NGINX example for this proxy: [`nginx/feedbackpilgrim-proxy.conf`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/blob/main/deploy/nginx/feedbackpilgrim-proxy.conf).

This example `Caddyfile` gets a wildcard certificate with a DNS challenge. It needs a Caddy build with the module of your DNS provider, here Cloudflare:

```text
feedback.example.com, *.feedback.example.com {
    tls {
        dns cloudflare {env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}
    }
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080
}
```

## Forwarded headers

The app reads these headers only from a trusted proxy: `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Port`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and the AWS ELB header. The rate limits and the logs use the client IP from these headers.

`TRUSTED_PROXIES` in `.env` sets the trusted proxies. It is a comma-separated list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges. If it is empty, the app trusts only the Cloudflare ranges in `config/trustedproxy.php`. Use the address that the app sees, not the public address of the proxy:

- If Caddy or NGINX runs on the Docker host, use the Docker network range: `TRUSTED_PROXIES=172.16.0.0/12`.
- If the proxy is on another server, use the private address of that server.
- If NGINX or Caddy runs PHP-FPM directly, without Docker, leave the value empty.

If the value is wrong, the app sees all the visitors with the IP of the proxy. Then the rate limits apply to all the visitors together, and the links in the emails can use `http` instead of `https`.

WARNING: Do not set `TRUSTED_PROXIES=*` when the app port is open to the internet. A client that can reach the port directly can then send a false IP, host or scheme.

The example above publishes the port on the loopback interface (`127.0.0.1`) of the host. Thus only a proxy on the same host can reach the port. The Compose files do the same. If the proxy is on another host, publish the port on all interfaces (with Compose, set `APP_BIND=0.0.0.0` in `.env`). Then allow the port only from the proxy with a firewall rule.

## Domain values

With `APP_DOMAIN` set, the app derives the other domain values. It uses `https` when `APP_URL` is not set. You need the table below only for an install without Docker, or to change a derived value:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `APP_URL` | `https://feedback.example.com` |
| `APP_DOMAIN` | `feedback.example.com` |
| `SESSION_DOMAIN` | `.feedback.example.com` |
| `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` | `true` |
| `SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS` | `feedback.example.com,*.feedback.example.com` |

The scheme of `APP_URL` is also the scheme of the links to the public sites. Read [Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md#domains).

## Health check

The route `/up` answers on any host. Use it for the health check of your proxy or your load balancer:

```bash
curl -fsS https://feedback.example.com/up
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/backups.md

# Backups

Feedback Pilgrim does not make backups by itself. Make them with the tools of your server.

Back up the database and the uploads each day. Keep the daily backups for 14 days. Also make a backup before each upgrade. Copy the backups to storage outside the server. Restore a backup to a test server one time each month, to make sure that the backups work.

## What to back up

With the default Docker install, back up one item: the `/data` volume. It holds the SQLite database, the generated secrets with `APP_KEY`, the uploads and the TLS certificates.

With MySQL or without Docker, back up these items:

| Item | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The database | MySQL. The `mysql` volume with Docker. | All the records: users, projects, posts, contacts, tokens and settings. |
| The uploads | `storage/app`. The `storage` volume with Docker. | Post attachments, comment photos, avatars and logos. |
| `.env` | The folder of the repository | `APP_KEY` and the other secrets. |

WARNING: Back up `APP_KEY` with the database. The app encrypts the identity secret of each project with `APP_KEY`. Without the same key, a restored database cannot decrypt the identity secrets, and the widget cannot verify the users.

Redis holds the cache, the sessions, the queued jobs and the last-login times of the contacts. If you lose Redis, the users must sign in again, and the queued jobs that did not run are lost. The `redis` volume keeps the data on disk.

## Back up the `/data` volume

These commands stop the container for a few seconds. A stopped container makes a consistent copy of the SQLite database.

1. Stop the container:

   ```bash
   docker stop feedbackpilgrim
   ```

2. Copy the volume to a file in the current folder:

   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v feedbackpilgrim:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
     tar czf /backup/feedbackpilgrim-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C /data .
   ```

3. Start the container:

   ```bash
   docker start feedbackpilgrim
   ```

4. Move the file to storage outside the server.

## Restore the `/data` volume

1. Remove the container and the volume:

   ```bash
   docker rm -f feedbackpilgrim
   docker volume rm feedbackpilgrim
   ```

2. Copy the backup into a new volume:

   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v feedbackpilgrim:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
     tar xzf /backup/feedbackpilgrim-2026-11-25.tar.gz -C /data
   ```

3. Start the container with the same command as before. The container reads `APP_KEY` from the volume.

## Back up the Compose stack with MySQL

Run these commands in the folder of the repository.

1. Export the database:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec -T mysql sh -c 'mysqldump --single-transaction -u"$MYSQL_USER" -p"$MYSQL_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"' > feedbackpilgrim.sql
   ```

2. Copy the uploads:

   ```bash
   docker compose cp web:/var/www/html/storage/app ./storage-app
   ```

3. Copy `.env` to a safe place.
4. Move the three items to storage outside the server.

The `MYSQL_USER`, `MYSQL_PASSWORD` and `MYSQL_DATABASE` variables are set inside the `mysql` container from your `.env`.

## Restore the Compose stack with MySQL

1. Start the stack with the `.env` from the backup:

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```

2. Import the database:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec -T mysql sh -c 'mysql -u"$MYSQL_USER" -p"$MYSQL_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"' < feedbackpilgrim.sql
   ```

3. Copy the uploads back:

   ```bash
   docker compose cp ./storage-app/. web:/var/www/html/storage/app
   ```

4. Give the files to the `www-data` user. The app runs as this user:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec -u root web chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/html/storage/app
   ```

5. Restart the app services:

   ```bash
   docker compose restart web queue scheduler
   ```

## Without Docker

Back up the same three items:

- Export the database with `mysqldump`.
- Copy the folder `storage/app`.
- Copy `.env`.

To restore, import the database, copy `storage/app` back, and run `php artisan fp:install --prepare` to create the storage link.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/queues-and-scheduler.md

# Queues and the scheduler

Feedback Pilgrim needs two processes in addition to the web server:

| Process | Command |
|---|---|
| Queue worker | `php artisan queue:work --tries=3` |
| Scheduler | `php artisan schedule:work` |

The Docker image runs both processes in the same container as the web server. You do not start them yourself. `php artisan fp:status` shows the last heartbeat of the queue and the last run of the scheduler.

Without Docker, run the two processes with systemd or Supervisor. Read [Run the processes without Docker](#run-the-processes-without-docker).

## What the queue runs

`QUEUE_CONNECTION` is `redis` in `.env.example`. The worker runs these jobs:

| Job | What it does | Tries |
|---|---|---|
| Notifications | All the emails to contacts and users. Read [Notifications and weekly reports](../using-feedback-pilgrim/notifications-and-weekly-reports.md). | 3 (from `--tries=3`) |
| `DeliverWebhook` | Sends one webhook event. | 3, with a wait of 10 seconds, then 60 seconds |
| `SendSlackMessage` | Posts one Slack message. | 3, with a wait of 10 seconds, then 60 seconds |
| `SyncContactAttributes` | Adds the new custom attribute keys of a contact to the attribute list of the project. | 3 (from `--tries=3`) |
| `CopyTestimonialAvatar` | Copies the avatar of one imported Senja testimonial to `storage/app/public`. It has 30 seconds. Read [Avatars of imported testimonials](../using-feedback-pilgrim/testimonials.md#avatars-of-imported-testimonials). | 1 |

If the worker stops, the app keeps the jobs in Redis. The emails, the webhooks, the Slack messages and the avatar copies run when the worker starts again.

The testimonial request email does not use the queue. The app sends it during the request that moves the post to a `complete` stage.

## The scheduler

The scheduler has two tasks:

| Task | When |
|---|---|
| `php artisan fp:weekly` | Every Monday at 09:00 UTC |
| `php artisan sending-domains:check` | Every 10 minutes |

`sending-domains:check` asks SES for the status of each pending sending domain. It also checks each verified domain again one time each day. It does not check a failed domain. Read [Send email from your domain](../using-feedback-pilgrim/sending-domain.md).

To see the tasks and the next run, run:

```bash
php artisan schedule:list
```

## Run the processes without Docker

1. Run `php artisan queue:work --tries=3` with a process manager, for example systemd or Supervisor. Restart it if it stops.
2. Run the scheduler. Use `php artisan schedule:work` with the process manager, or add a cron entry that runs the scheduler each minute:

   ```text
   * * * * * cd /var/www/feedbackpilgrim && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
   ```

3. After each deploy, restart the worker:

   ```bash
   php artisan queue:restart
   ```

The [`deploy/`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/tree/main/deploy) folder of the app repository has example files for the two processes. Use the systemd units or the Supervisor file, not both:

- [`systemd/feedbackpilgrim-queue.service`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/blob/main/deploy/systemd/feedbackpilgrim-queue.service)
- [`systemd/feedbackpilgrim-scheduler.service`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/blob/main/deploy/systemd/feedbackpilgrim-scheduler.service)
- [`supervisor/feedbackpilgrim.conf`](https://github.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim/blob/main/deploy/supervisor/feedbackpilgrim.conf)

The app has one queue, `default`, on the connection that `QUEUE_CONNECTION` sets. Run one worker. A job has 60 seconds, the default `--timeout` of `queue:work`. The examples give a stopped worker 70 seconds to finish its job.

## Logs in Docker

The queue worker and the scheduler write to the log of the container:

```bash
docker logs feedbackpilgrim
```

## Failed jobs

A job that fails all its tries goes to the `failed_jobs` table.

To list the failed jobs, run:

```bash
php artisan queue:failed
```

To try all of them again, run:

```bash
php artisan queue:retry all
```

With Docker, run the commands in the container, for example `docker exec feedbackpilgrim php artisan queue:failed`.

A webhook delivery that fails also shows in the delivery log on **Settings > Webhooks**.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/mail.md

# Mail

Feedback Pilgrim sends emails to users and contacts: password resets, notifications, weekly reports and testimonial requests. Read [Notifications and weekly reports](../using-feedback-pilgrim/notifications-and-weekly-reports.md) for the list.

Most emails go through the queue. Thus the queue worker must run. Read [Queues and the scheduler](queues-and-scheduler.md).

## The sender

| Variable | Default in `.env.example` | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` | `"feedback@example.com"` | The sender address. |
| `MAIL_FROM_NAME` | `"${APP_NAME}"` | The sender name. |

## SMTP

SMTP is the default mailer.

| Variable | Default in `.env.example` |
|---|---|
| `MAIL_MAILER` | `smtp` |
| `MAIL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |
| `MAIL_PORT` | `587` |
| `MAIL_USERNAME` | `null` |
| `MAIL_PASSWORD` | `null` |

The port sets the TLS mode. Port `465` uses implicit TLS. Each other port, for example `587`, starts without TLS and uses STARTTLS when the server offers it.

To set the TLS mode yourself, set `MAIL_SCHEME` to `smtp` (STARTTLS) or `smtps` (implicit TLS). The app does not read the old Laravel value for the encryption. A change to that value has no effect.

## Mailgun

1. Set `MAIL_MAILER=mailgun`.
2. Set `MAILGUN_DOMAIN` and `MAILGUN_SECRET`.
3. To use another Mailgun API host, set `MAILGUN_ENDPOINT`. The default is `api.mailgun.net`.

The app has the package `symfony/mailgun-mailer`.

## Amazon SES

1. Set `MAIL_MAILER=ses`.
2. Set `AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
3. Set `AWS_SES_REGION`.

The app has the AWS SDK for PHP.

| Variable | If it is empty, the app uses | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | The access key for SES. |
| `AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | The secret key for SES. |
| `AWS_SES_REGION` | `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, then `us-east-1` | The SES region. |
| `AWS_SES_CONFIGURATION_SET` | No configuration set | Optional. The SES configuration set for each email from the `ses` mailer. |

An instance that used only the `AWS_*` values before keeps working. The `AWS_SES_*` values are optional.

## Sending domains for projects

A project can send the emails to its contacts from its own domain. Read [Send email from your domain](../using-feedback-pilgrim/sending-domain.md) for the steps of the user.

The SES account of the instance sends for all projects. The projects do not give AWS keys. The emails from a verified domain always use the `ses` mailer. The other emails use `MAIL_MAILER`, so `MAIL_MAILER` can stay `smtp`.

### Prepare the SES account

1. Create an IAM user for the app. Give it only these actions:
   - `ses:CreateEmailIdentity`
   - `ses:GetEmailIdentity`
   - `ses:DeleteEmailIdentity`
   - `ses:PutEmailIdentityMailFromAttributes`
   - `ses:TagResource`
   - `ses:SendRawEmail`
2. Request SES production access from AWS. In the sandbox, SES sends only to verified addresses, also from a verified domain.
3. Turn on the account-level suppression list for bounces and complaints. All projects share the reputation of the account.
4. Set `AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SES_REGION`.
5. Make sure that the scheduler runs. Read [Queues and the scheduler](queues-and-scheduler.md).
6. If the app runs on more than one server, set `CACHE_DRIVER` to `redis` or `database`.
7. Give the queue worker 512 MB of memory or more, for example `php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --memory=512`. The AWS SDK uses more memory.

If the scheduler does not run, the app checks a domain only when a user clicks **Check now**.

The app holds a cache lock for each domain while it changes the SES identity. A `file` cache locks on one server only. Thus more than one server needs a shared cache store.

### SES identities

- The app creates one SES identity for each connected domain. It gives each identity the tag `app=feedbackpilgrim`.
- The app deletes an identity only if the identity has this tag and no project has the domain. It never uses an identity that another app made.
- If the SES account already has an identity for a domain without this tag, the connection fails with "This domain is already connected."
- If SES refuses a request, the page shows "Amazon SES could not complete the request. Try again in a few minutes." The log has the AWS error code.

## Postmark

The app does not support Postmark. The configuration has a `postmark` mailer and `POSTMARK_TOKEN`, but the mailer needs the package `symfony/postmark-mailer`. The app does not include this package. If you set `MAIL_MAILER=postmark`, each email fails.

## Test without a mail server

Set `MAIL_MAILER=log`. The app then writes each email to the log, and sends nothing. Use this mode only for a test.

## If the instance has no mail

Without mail, a user cannot reset a password with the form, and contacts get no notifications. To set a password in the terminal, read [Recover access](recover-access.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/accounts-and-registration.md

# Accounts and registration

## The owner

An owner runs the instance. Only an owner sees the **Admin** link and can open `/admin`. Other users get 404 there. Read [The admin area](../using-feedback-pilgrim/admin-area.md).

An instance can have more than one owner. Nobody can deactivate an owner.

## Create the first owner

On an empty instance, two ways create the owner, the first project and the admin contact of the owner:

- The setup page at `/setup`. Read [Install with Docker](../getting-started/installation-docker.md#the-setup-url).
- The command `php artisan fp:install`.

Both ways mark the email of the owner as verified, and finish the onboarding.

### The `fp:install` command

```bash
php artisan fp:install
```

The command asks for each value that you do not give as an option:

| Option | Rules |
|---|---|
| `--name` | Required, 255 characters or fewer |
| `--email` | Required, a lowercase email, unique |
| `--project` | The name of the first project. 255 characters or fewer. |
| `--subdomain` | The subdomain of the first project. Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. Not reserved, unique. |

The command needs no password. It shows a login link that works one time, for 60 minutes. After the login, the owner can set a password on the profile page. The old options `--password` and `--client-name` still work, but they are deprecated.

If the instance has an owner with the same email, the command changes nothing, shows a new login link and exits with code 0. If the instance has users but this email is not an owner, the command stops with the error code `instance_has_owner` and exits with code 3.

At the end, the command shows the URL of the dashboard and of the public site.

For a script or an AI agent, add `--json --no-interaction`. With `--json`, the command prints one JSON object with a one-time `login_url`. With `--with-token=<name>`, it also makes an API token and returns the `claude mcp add` and `codex mcp add` commands. In this mode, a second run makes no change, returns `"status":"exists"` and exits with code 0. Read the `INSTALL.md` file of the app repository for the full agent procedure.

The command also has two other modes:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--prepare` | Creates only the storage link. Creates no account. The Docker image runs this at start. |
| `--promote=<email>` | Makes the existing user with this email an owner. Creates no account. |

## Make a user an owner

```bash
php artisan fp:install --promote=person@example.com
```

With Docker:

```bash
docker exec feedbackpilgrim php artisan fp:install --promote=person@example.com
```

## Registration modes

The instance has two registration modes:

| Mode | Effect |
|---|---|
| Closed | Nobody can sign up. `/register` returns 404. This is the default. |
| Open | Anyone can sign up at `/register`. A new user then creates a project. |

`REGISTRATION_ENABLED` gives the mode until the owner sets one:

- `REGISTRATION_ENABLED=false` gives the closed mode.
- `REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true` gives the open mode.

To change the mode, open **Admin > Settings**. The mode that the owner saves stays in the `instance_settings` table. It wins over `REGISTRATION_ENABLED`.

## Invitations

Feedback Pilgrim has no invitations. On a closed instance, only the setup page and `fp:install` create accounts. No screen adds a user to an existing project.

## Email verification

The app has the email verification routes of Laravel Breeze, but no page requires a verified email.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/recover-access.md

# Recover access

The "forgot password" form sends an email. If the instance has no mail, or if a user cannot read the email, use the commands on this page.

With Docker, put `docker exec feedbackpilgrim` before each command, for example `docker exec feedbackpilgrim php artisan fp:user:list`. With Docker Compose, use `docker compose exec web`.

## Find a user

```bash
php artisan fp:user:list --search=person
```

The command lists the users with these columns: ID, name, email, projects, owner, status (`active` or `deactivated`) and the date of creation. `--search` finds the text in the name or the email. Without `--search`, the command lists all the users.

## Set a new password

```bash
php artisan fp:user:password person@example.com
```

The command asks for the new password two times.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--password=<new password>` | Sets this password, without a prompt. Use it in a script. |
| `--generate` | Makes a random password of 32 letters and digits, and shows it one time. |

You cannot use `--password` and `--generate` together. If the command cannot prompt, give one of them.

The new password must obey the same rules as the web forms.

After the change, the command:

- ends all the "Remember me" logins of the user,
- removes the web sessions of the user, if `SESSION_DRIVER` is `database`.

With the `redis` session driver, the command cannot find the sessions of one user. An open web session stays open until it expires (`SESSION_LIFETIME`) or the user logs out.

WARNING: The command shows a generated password in the terminal. Copy it at once, and clear the terminal history if other people can read it.

## Lost setup URL

While the instance has no user, show the setup URL again:

```bash
php artisan fp:setup-url
```

With Docker, the log of the container also shows the URL: `docker logs feedbackpilgrim`.

If a user exists, the command says `An account already exists. The setup page is closed.`

## No owner can sign in

Make another user an owner:

```bash
php artisan fp:install --promote=person@example.com
```

Then set a password for that user with `fp:user:password` if necessary.

## A deactivated user

An owner can reactivate a user in **Admin > Users**. Read [The admin area](../using-feedback-pilgrim/admin-area.md#deactivate-a-user).

## Two-factor authentication

Feedback Pilgrim has no two-factor authentication. Thus no reset of a second factor is necessary.

## A lost `APP_KEY`

If you lose `APP_KEY`, and you set a new key:

- The setup URL changes.
- The sign-in links that the app sent to contacts stop working.
- The app cannot decrypt the identity secret of each project. The widget then refuses each `userHash` with 403.
- The users must sign in again.

To make a new identity secret after a key change, do these steps in each project:

1. Sign in as a user of the project.
2. Open **Settings > Embed Widget**. The page says that the app cannot read the identity secret.
3. Click **Regenerate secret**.
4. Put the new secret in the server of your app.

No command makes new secrets for all projects together.

To prevent this, back up `.env`. Read [Backups](backups.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/self-hosting/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

## Run the doctor

`fp:doctor` checks the database, the migrations, the queue, the scheduler, the storage link, the mail settings and the domain values. For each problem, it gives the fix.

```bash
docker exec feedbackpilgrim php artisan fp:doctor
```

- Add `--fix` to apply the safe fixes, for example a missing storage link.
- Add `--json` to get one JSON object for a script or an AI agent.
- Run `fp:status --json` for a short summary of the instance.

## Read the log

With the Docker image, the log goes to the container log:

```bash
docker logs --tail 100 feedbackpilgrim
```

With Docker Compose, read the log of the `web` service:

```bash
docker compose logs web
```

Without Docker, the default `LOG_STACK=daily` writes the log to `storage/logs`.

## The installer stops

The installer prints an `Error:` line and a `Fix:` line. Do the fix, then run the installer again. The full log is in `/tmp/feedbackpilgrim-install.log`.

| Error | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Docker is not installed.` | Install Docker with `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com \| sh`. |
| `Your user cannot use Docker.` | Run the installer with `sudo`, or add your user to the `docker` group. |
| `Port 80 is in use.` | Another web server uses the port. Stop it, or read [Reverse proxy and TLS](reverse-proxy-and-tls.md#your-own-proxy). |
| `The container stopped.` | Read `docker logs feedbackpilgrim`. |

## The setup page asks for the setup URL

The page "Find the setup URL" shows when you open `/setup` without the correct token. The token is in the setup URL. Run `docker logs feedbackpilgrim` or `php artisan fp:setup-url`, then open the URL from the output.

If the token in the URL is not correct, `APP_KEY` changed after the log printed the URL. Run `fp:setup-url` again.

## The public site of a project returns 404

1. Make sure that the DNS has a wildcard record for `APP_DOMAIN`, for example `*.feedback.example.com`.
2. Make sure that the reverse proxy sends the wildcard to the app, with the original `Host` header.
3. Make sure that `APP_DOMAIN` is the parent of the project host. For `acme.feedback.example.com`, `APP_DOMAIN` is `feedback.example.com`.
4. Make sure that the subdomain is the slug of a project, and is not reserved.
5. Make sure that the project has at least one active user. If every user of the project is deactivated, the public site returns 404.

## The dashboard does not load, or `/setup` sends you to the wrong host

The dashboard routes answer only on the host of `APP_URL`. Make sure that `APP_URL` has the host that you open in the browser.

## The Public Site link does not sign you in

The public site reads the dashboard session through the cookie domain.

1. Make sure that `SESSION_DOMAIN` starts with a dot, for example `.feedback.example.com`.
2. If `APP_URL` uses `https`, make sure that `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` is `true`.
3. For local work on `http`, set `SESSION_DOMAIN=null` and `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false`.

## Links use `http` instead of `https`

1. Make sure that `APP_URL` starts with `https://`.
2. Make sure that the reverse proxy sends `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

## The widget gets 401, 403 or 422

| Status | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | The `data-client` value is not a publishable key of a project, or every user of the project is deactivated. | Copy the publishable key from **Settings > Embed Widget**. |
| `403` | The `userHash` is wrong, or it is missing and verification is required. | Make the hash from the lowercase, trimmed email with the current identity secret. |
| `422` | The call has no contact email. | Send `contact.email`. |

Read [The embeddable widget](../using-feedback-pilgrim/widget.md).

## The widget does not sign in an existing user

Without a valid `userHash`, the widget does not sign in a contact that exists already. Send `userHash`. Read [Identity verification](../using-feedback-pilgrim/widget.md#identity-verification).

## The API or the MCP server returns 401

1. Make sure that you send the full token, with the part before the `|`.
2. Make sure that you send `Accept: application/json`.
3. Make sure that the user of the token is active, and is still a member of the project.
4. Make sure that nobody deleted the token in **Settings > API Tokens**.

## Emails do not arrive

1. Make sure that the queue worker runs. Run `php artisan fp:status` and read the queue heartbeat.
2. Look for failed jobs with `php artisan queue:failed`.
3. Make sure that the `MAIL_*` values are correct. Read [Mail](mail.md).

## Webhooks or Slack messages do not arrive

1. Make sure that the queue worker runs.
2. Open **Settings > Webhooks** and read the delivery log of the webhook.
3. Make sure that the webhook is active and has the event.
4. If the receiver refuses the requests with `401`, make sure that it verifies `X-FeedbackPilgrim-Signature-V2` with the timestamp. Read [Verify the signature](../using-feedback-pilgrim/webhooks-and-slack.md#verify-the-signature).

## The weekly report does not arrive

1. Make sure that the scheduler runs. With Docker, look at the `scheduler` service.
2. Run `php artisan schedule:list`. The list must show `fp:weekly`.
3. Remember that the time is 09:00 UTC on Monday.

## A change in `.env` has no effect

The app caches the configuration. With `docker run`, remove the container and start it again with the new values. With Docker Compose, run `docker compose up -d`. Without Docker, run `php artisan optimize`, then `php artisan queue:restart`.

## The container is not healthy

1. Read `docker logs feedbackpilgrim`, or `docker compose logs web` with Compose.
2. If the log shows a database error, make sure that `DB_PASSWORD` in `.env` is the password of the `mysql` volume. MySQL sets the password only when it creates the volume.
3. Open `/up` on the host. It must return status 200.

## An uploaded file returns 404

The app serves uploads through the link `public/storage`. Create the link:

```bash
php artisan fp:install --prepare
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/contributing/architecture.md

# Architecture

This page is a short map of the code. The file `ARCHITECTURE.md` in the app repository has the full details. Read it before a large change.

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Framework | Laravel 13 with the streamlined skeleton, PHP 8.3 |
| Frontend | Vue 3, Tailwind CSS 4, Quill, Chart.js |
| Build | Vite 8, with two build targets |
| Auth | Session guards `web` (users) and `contact` (contacts), and Laravel Sanctum for API tokens |
| Uploads | Spatie Media Library on the `public` disk |
| MCP | `laravel/mcp` |
| Audit | `spatie/laravel-activitylog` |

`bootstrap/app.php` holds the routing, the middleware aliases and the exception handling. The app has no `app/Http/Kernel.php` and no `app/Console/Kernel.php`.

## Request surfaces

The same data goes through several surfaces. The code groups the routes, the controllers and the views by surface.

| Surface | Host | Auth | Code | Routes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | The host of `APP_URL` | `auth` (user) | `PostController`, `ReleaseNoteController` and others | `routes/web.php`, `routes/auth.php` |
| Admin area | The host of `APP_URL`, `/admin` | `owner` | `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\*` | `routes/web.php` |
| Public site | A project subdomain | `auth:contact` or none | `Client*` controllers | `routes/web.php` |
| Iframes | A project subdomain | None | `Iframe*` controllers | `routes/iframe.php` |
| Widget API | Any host, `/api/v1` | Publishable key (`widget_client`) or the project host | `App\Http\Controllers\Api\*` | `routes/api.php` |
| REST API | Any host, `/api/public/v1` | Sanctum token and `api_client` | `App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1\Public\*` | `routes/public-api.php` |
| MCP server | Any host, `/mcp` | Sanctum token, `api_client` and `throttle:mcp` | `App\Mcp\Servers\PublicServer` and `App\Mcp\Tools\*` | `routes/ai.php` |
| Guides and API reference | The host of `APP_URL`, `/documentation` | None | `DocumentationController` | `routes/web.php` |

## Shared logic of the REST API and the MCP server

The REST API and the MCP server call the same code:

- **Actions** in `app/Actions/<Resource>/` hold the read and write behavior. Each action is an invokable class that takes a `ClientContext` and an input array.
- **Rules** in `app/Rules/Public/*Rules.php` are the only source of validation for each resource.
- `App\Support\ClientContext` resolves the project and the user from the token. A request never gives the project. The dashboard calls some actions too (the release note edit page, the tag rename and delete). It builds the context from the session project with `ClientContext::fromDashboard()`.

The controllers and the MCP tools are thin. A contract test (`tests/Feature/Mcp/ContractTest.php`) makes sure that the rules, the MCP tool schemas and `public/docs/openapi.json` agree.

## Tenancy

The project (`Client`) is the tenant root. Each domain record except `User` has a `client_id`.

| Surface | How the app finds the project |
|---|---|
| Public site and iframes | `IdentifyClientMiddleware` reads the host. A subdomain of `APP_DOMAIN` is the slug of a project. Another host gets 404. Custom domains are not supported. |
| Dashboard | `GrabClientIdFromSessionMiddleware` reads `fp_client_id` from the session, or uses the first project of the user. Request input never sets the project. |
| Widget `init` | `IdentifyWidgetClientMiddleware` reads the publishable key from the bearer header. |
| REST API and MCP | `ApiClientMiddleware` builds a `ClientContext` from the `client_id` of the Sanctum token. |

## Domain model

```text
User ──many-to-many (client_user)── Client
                                      ├─ Contact ──< Vote, Comment, Post, Testimonial
                                      ├─ Board ──< Post
                                      ├─ Stage ──< Post
                                      ├─ Post (tags, votes, comments, attachments)
                                      ├─ ReleaseNote (tags, votes, comments)
                                      ├─ Testimonial (votes, comments)
                                      ├─ Tag (on Post, Contact and ReleaseNote)
                                      ├─ ClientSetting (key and value)
                                      ├─ ContactAttribute (custom attribute names)
                                      ├─ Webhook ──< WebhookDelivery
                                      ├─ SendingDomain (one for each client)
                                      └─ WeeklyReport
```

- `Comment` and `Vote` are polymorphic across Post, ReleaseNote and Testimonial.
- The stage of a post is the source of truth. The `status` field mirrors it. `Post::booted()` keeps the two in step.
- `InstanceSetting` holds the settings of the instance, for example the registration mode. It has no `client_id`.

## Background work

| Kind | Classes |
|---|---|
| Jobs | `SyncContactAttributes`, `DeliverWebhook`, `SendSlackMessage` |
| Observer | `ContactObserver` queues `SyncContactAttributes` when the metadata changes. |
| Event and listener | `PostCompletedEvent` and `RequestTestimonial` |
| Notifications | `PostCommented`, `PostCompletedNotification`, `PostStatusChangedNotification`, `PostCreatedByContact`, `ReleaseNoteCommented`, `WeeklyReportNotification` |
| Schedule | `fp:weekly` every Monday at 09:00, and `sending-domains:check` every 10 minutes, in `routes/console.php` |

`App\Support\PostStageTransition` runs a stage change from the dashboard, and a status change from the REST API or the MCP server (`UpdatePost`). It sends the notifications, the webhook events and the Slack message.

`Client::mailSender()` picks the mailer and the From address of each email to contacts. The actions in `app/Actions/SendingDomains/` are the only code that changes the SES identities of the sending domains.

## Build targets

`npm run build` makes two bundles:

1. The dashboard (`vite.config.js`): `resources/css/app.css` and `resources/js/app.js` to `public/build/`.
2. The widget (`vite.config.external-script.js`): `resources/js/pilgrim.js` to `public/pilgrim.js`. The widget reads the server URL from its own script tag, so one build works on every host.

## Key folders

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `app/Actions` | The shared logic of the REST API and the MCP server |
| `app/Console/Commands` | The `fp:*` commands |
| `app/Http/Controllers` | The controllers of each surface |
| `app/Mcp` | The MCP server, the tools and the response helpers |
| `app/Models` | The domain models |
| `app/Rules/Public` | The validation rules of the REST API and the MCP server |
| `app/Support` | Helpers, for example `ClientContext`, `PostMerger` and `WebhookDispatcher` |
| `deploy/docker` | The start script of the Docker image |
| `public/docs/openapi.json` | The OpenAPI document |
| `resources/js` | `app.js`, `pilgrim.js`, the Vue components |
| `routes` | `web`, `auth`, `api`, `public-api`, `iframe`, `ai` and `console` |

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/contributing/development-setup.md

# Development setup

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3 with the `pdo_mysql`, `redis`, `gd` and `exif` extensions
- Composer
- Node.js 24
- MySQL
- Redis

The tests do not need MySQL or Redis. Read [Testing](testing.md).

## Install

1. Clone the repository and go into its folder.
2. Install the dependencies:

   ```bash
   composer install
   npm install
   ```

3. Create the environment file and the key:

   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   php artisan key:generate
   ```

4. Set these values in `.env`:

   | Variable | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `APP_ENV` | `local` |
   | `APP_DEBUG` | `true` |
   | `APP_DOMAIN` | `localhost` |
   | `APP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` |
   | `SESSION_DOMAIN` | `null` |
   | `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` | `false` |

5. Create the tables and the example data:

   ```bash
   php artisan migrate --seed
   ```

6. Start Vite:

   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

7. In a second terminal, start the app:

   ```bash
   php artisan serve
   ```

8. If your change uses queued jobs, start a worker in a third terminal:

   ```bash
   php artisan queue:work
   ```

## The example data

The seeders create the user `test@example.com` with the password `password`.

Browsers send `*.localhost` to your own computer. Thus the public site of a seeded project is at `http://<slug>.localhost:8000`.

## Commands

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `php artisan test` | Run all the PHP tests. |
| `php artisan test --filter=SomeTest` | Run one test class or method. |
| `npm run test:js` | Run the JavaScript tests. |
| `vendor/bin/pint` | Format the PHP code. |
| `npm run dev` | Start Vite with hot reload. |
| `npm run build` | Build the dashboard assets (`public/build`) and the widget (`public/pilgrim.js`). |
| `php artisan migrate` | Run the migrations. |
| `php artisan db:seed` | Add the example data. |

## Rules for a change

The app repository has its own `CONTRIBUTING.md`. These are the main rules:

- Write the test first when you add behavior.
- Format the PHP code with Laravel Pint.
- Use explicit return types and parameter types.
- Use `env()` only in `config/`. Use `config()` everywhere else.
- Style the UI with Tailwind CSS classes and the `fp-*` theme tokens.
- Read `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` before a UI change.
- Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` in the same pull request when a change affects the architecture. Examples are the data model, a request surface, the tenancy rules, an auth guard and a build target.
- Do not use Vue text interpolation in Blade views. Use props or a `.vue` component. The test `tests/js/server-template.test.mjs` checks this rule.

## Security problems

Do not open a public issue for a security problem. Use the security advisory form of the repository.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/contributing/testing.md

# Testing

## Run the tests

Run all the PHP tests:

```bash
php artisan test
```

Run one test class or method:

```bash
php artisan test --filter=WebhookTest
```

Run the JavaScript tests:

```bash
npm run test:js
```

Format the PHP code:

```bash
vendor/bin/pint
```

## The test environment

The tests use PHPUnit and the values in `phpunit.xml`. You do not need MySQL or Redis.

| Variable | Value in `phpunit.xml` |
|---|---|
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `sqlite` |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `:memory:` |
| `CACHE_DRIVER` | `array` |
| `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `sync` |
| `SESSION_DRIVER` | `array` |
| `MAIL_MAILER` | `array` |
| `APP_DOMAIN` | `localhost` |
| `APP_URL` | `http://localhost` |
| `REGISTRATION_ENABLED` | `false` |
| `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` | `4` |

## Where the tests are

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `tests/Feature` | Request and response tests, for example the public API, the widget, the MCP server, the tenancy rules and the commands. |
| `tests/Unit` | Tests for classes without HTTP, for example the actions, the rules and the models. |
| `tests/js` | Node tests for the widget and the Blade templates. |

## Tests that guard a rule

| Test | Rule |
|---|---|
| `tests/Feature/Mcp/ContractTest.php` | The validation rules, the MCP tool schemas and `public/docs/openapi.json` agree. |
| `tests/Feature/RouteNamesTest.php` | Each route name is unique, so that `php artisan optimize` can cache the routes. |
| `tests/Feature/DocumentationTest.php` | The guides and the API reference at `/documentation` work. |
| `tests/js/pilgrim-origin.test.mjs` | The widget builds the `init` URL from the host of its own script tag. |
| `tests/js/server-template.test.mjs` | The Blade views use no Vue text interpolation. |

## Write a test

- Every change needs a test. Write the test first when you add behavior.
- Put request and response tests in `tests/Feature`. Put tests for classes without HTTP in `tests/Unit`.
- Use the model factories and the `RefreshDatabase` trait.
- Name a test after the behavior that it checks, for example `test_onboarding_creates_the_admin_contact_for_the_new_client`.

## Before a pull request

Make sure that these commands pass:

```bash
php artisan test
vendor/bin/pint --test
npm run build
```

## The CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on each push to `main` and on each pull request. It has four jobs:

| Job | What it runs |
|---|---|
| Code style (Pint) | `vendor/bin/pint --test` on PHP 8.3 |
| PHP tests | `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, then `php artisan test` |
| JS build | `npm ci`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:js` on Node.js 24. Then it makes sure that `public/pilgrim.js` and `public/build/manifest.json` exist. |
| API docs | `composer api-docs`, then `git diff --exit-code docs/api public/docs/openapi.json`. The job fails when the generated API files are not current. |

If you change `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, run `composer api-docs` and commit the generated files.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amedina068/feedbackpilgrim-docs/main/contributing/release-process.md

# Release process

The `main` branch of the app has a changelog and a workflow that publishes the Docker image, but no version tags yet. This page explains the release notes and the changelog. It also has the facts that the code gives about versions, and the questions for the maintainer.

## Release notes

[Release notes](../getting-started/release-notes.md) in this docs repository holds the release notes of Feedback Pilgrim. The app repository has no release notes file.

The release notes of the app are not the release notes feature of Feedback Pilgrim. That feature lets a project publish its own changelog. Read [Release notes](../using-feedback-pilgrim/release-notes.md).

### In a pull request of the app

A pull request with a change that users can see has a `## Release note` section in its body. Write one or two short sentences in plain text. Tell the user what changed and what to do.

```markdown
## Release note

The weekly report now covers the previous week, Monday to Sunday.
```

A pull request without a change for users has no `## Release note` section.

### When a release goes out

1. Collect the `## Release note` sections of the merged pull requests.
2. Open `getting-started/release-notes.md` in the docs repository.
3. Find the heading of the release date, for example `## November 18, 2026`. If it does not exist, add it above the other dates.
4. Add one bullet for each note. Copy the text of the note as it is.
5. Open a pull request in the docs repository.

### Rules

- Write plain text. Do not use Markdown links or HTML in a note.
- Write one change in each bullet.
- Keep the newest date first. Do not add a second heading for the same date.
- Do not change old notes.

## Versions and images: what the code gives

- The project uses Semantic Versioning. `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog. The first version, `0.1.0`, is in the changelog, but it has no release date yet.
- If a pull request changes the behavior for users, it adds one line under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`. The sections are `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed` and `Security`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of each version of the code. The release notes page of the docs lists the changes that users can see, by date. A change for users goes in `CHANGELOG.md` and in the `## Release note` section of the pull request.
- A push of a tag that starts with `v`, for example `v1.2.3`, starts `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`. A push to a branch or a pull request does not publish an image.
- The workflow builds the image for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` and pushes it to `ghcr.io/<owner>/feedbackpilgrim`.
- The tag `v1.2.3` gives the image tags `1.2.3`, `1.2` and `latest`. The major tag `1` starts at `1.0.0`, so a `v0` tag gives no major tag.
- A pre-release tag, for example `v1.3.0-rc.1`, gives only the image tag `1.3.0-rc.1`. The tag `latest` stays on the last stable release.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on each push to `main` and on each pull request. It runs Pint, the PHP tests, the JS build and the JS tests, and a check that the API docs files are current.
- `SECURITY.md` says that only the latest release gets security fixes.
- The MCP server reports the version `1.0.0`. The value is in the `#[Version]` attribute of `App\Mcp\Servers\PublicServer`.
- The OpenAPI document reports the version `1.0.0` in `info.version`.
- The REST API has the version in its path: `/api/public/v1`.
- The `web` service runs the new migrations at start. Thus an update is `git pull` and `docker compose up -d --build`. Read [Upgrading](../getting-started/upgrading.md).
